name: Ezekiel
sourceNote: Written freshly, thought for thought, from the oldest Hebrew, Greek, and Aramaic witnesses (the Masoretic Text with the Dead Sea Scrolls, the Septuagint, and the Samaritan Pentateuch). © 2026 Jose Santiago. All rights reserved.

verses.text: On the fifth day of the fourth month (in June–July),{a} in the thirtieth year,{b} I sat among the exiles near the Chebar canal.{c} Heaven split open, and God showed me visions.
The fifth day of that month fell in the fifth year since King Jehoiachin had been taken away as a captive.{d}
There in Chaldean country, by the Chebar canal, Yahweh spoke to the priest Ezekiel,{e} the son of Buzi.{f} The power of Yahweh came on him there.
A storm wind swept down from the north. I saw a giant cloud flashing with fire, ringed by bright light. Deep inside the fire, something glowed like shining metal.{g}
Out of the fire came four creatures that were alive. They looked something like people,
Each of them owned four faces, and each owned four wings.
The legs were straight. The feet looked like calf hooves, and they sparkled like polished bronze.
Under the wings, on each of the four sides, were hands like human hands. All four creatures had faces and wings,
Wing touched wing from one creature to the next. As they traveled, they never turned. Each simply moved forward.
Look at the four faces. A human face looked out the front. A lion’s face was on the right. An ox’s face was on the left. An eagle’s face was at the back.
That described their faces. Above, each creature stretched out two wings to meet the wings of its neighbors. It used its other pair to cover its own body.
Wherever the spirit{h} led, the creatures followed, straight ahead, with no turning.
Among the creatures moved what seemed to be burning coals or flaming torches. They drifted back and forth. The fire glowed bright, and bolts of lightning shot out of it.
The creatures themselves raced back and forth, as fast as lightning flashes.{i}
While I was looking at the creatures, I saw a wheel on the ground beside each of the four of them.
The wheels were made like this. They sparkled like a gem of golden-green color.{j} All four looked the same. Each wheel seemed to have a second wheel crossing through its middle.
They could roll in any of the four directions without turning around.
The rims were very high, and they were frightening. All around, the rims of the four wheels were full of eyes.
As the creatures traveled, the wheels traveled beside them. As the creatures lifted off the ground, the wheels lifted too.
Wherever the spirit led, they went, and the wheels were lifted up beside them, for the creature’s spirit lived in the wheels.{k}

The wheels copied the creatures. If the creatures went, the wheels went. If the creatures paused, the wheels paused. If the creatures rose, the wheels rose, since the creature’s spirit lived in the wheels.
Above the creatures’ heads was something like a dome. It glittered like ice and was awesome to see.{l} It spread out over their heads.
Under the dome, the creatures held out their wings straight, so that each touched the next. Each creature also used two wings to cover its body.
When they moved, I could hear their wings. The sound was like rushing floodwater, like the voice of Shaddai,{m} or like the noise of a great army. When they stopped, they folded their wings.
Then a voice sounded from above the dome over their heads, while they stood with their wings folded.
High over the dome there was a throne that looked like deep blue stone.{n} Seated on it was a shape like a man.
Above His waist, He gleamed like shining metal, as if flames were wrapped around Him. Below His waist, He looked like fire. A bright glow surrounded Him.

Think of a rainbow after rain, shining in the clouds. That is how bright the glow around Him was. This was the glory of Yahweh as I saw it. I dropped to the ground on my face, and then I heard a voice speak.

notes.text: The Hebrew says “in the fourth month, on the fifth day of the month.” Months here are counted from spring.
It is not clear what year this counts. It may be Ezekiel’s age, since priests began their work at thirty. It may be some other starting point.
The Hebrew word can also mean “river.” The Chebar was a canal near Nippur in Babylonia.
This was in 593 BC. Jehoiachin was taken to Babylon in 597 BC.
Ezekiel means “God makes strong” or “may God make strong.”
Buzi may mean “my scorn.” The meaning is not certain.
The Hebrew word is hashmal, a rare word of uncertain meaning. The Greek has “amber.” The same word is in verse 27.
The word can also mean “wind.” This is also true in verse 20.
Verse 14 is not found in the Greek (Septuagint).
The Hebrew word is tarshish, a gem of uncertain kind, maybe beryl or topaz.
The Hebrew has “the spirit of the living creature.” The word “creature” is singular here.
The Hebrew word for “dome” can also mean “platform” or “expanse.” It is the same word as in Genesis 1:6.
Shaddai is a name for God. It is often translated “the Almighty.” Its first meaning is uncertain.
The Hebrew word is sappir, probably lapis lazuli, a deep blue stone.

verses.text: God spoke to me: “Mortal one,{a} get up on your feet. I have words for you.”
While He was still speaking, the Spirit came into me. I was set upright, and I listened closely.
“Mortal one,” He said, “Israel is where I am sending you. That people has turned on Me. Their fathers fought against Me, and so do their children, right up to this day.
Their faces are hard, and their hearts will not bend. You are going to them with this message: ‘The Lord Yahweh says so.’
Maybe they will listen, and maybe not, for they rebel against Me. Either way they will learn that a prophet has been among them.

Do not fear them, mortal one. Do not fear their talk, even if you seem to be sitting in thorn bushes or on scorpions. Their words need not frighten you, and their glares need not shake you. They rebel against Me.
Speak My words to them, listening or not. They are rebels.
As for you, mortal one, hear what I say. Do not rebel like those rebels. Open your mouth and eat the food I hand you.”
Then I saw a hand reaching toward me. Inside it lay a scroll.
He unrolled it before my eyes. Both sides were covered in writing. It was all sad songs, weeping, and warnings of disaster.

notes.text: The Hebrew is ben adam, “son of a human being.” It means “human one” or “mortal.” It reminds Ezekiel that he is only a man, and God is God. God calls him this about ninety times in this book.

verses.text: God said to me, “Son of man, eat what you have been given. Eat this scroll. Then go and speak to Israel.”
I opened wide, and He put the scroll in my mouth.
“Mortal one,” He said, “let this scroll I am handing over feed your stomach until you are full.” So I swallowed it, and honey could not have tasted sweeter.
He said, “Son of man, go to Israel now. Tell them My words.
I am not sending you to people with a strange speech or a language that is hard to learn. I am sending you to Israel.
You are not going to many nations whose words you could not follow. If I had sent you to them, they would have listened to you.
Israel, however, will not listen to you, because Israel will not listen to Me. Every one of them is stubborn and hard-hearted.
So I will make you just as tough as they are. Your face will be as hard as theirs.
I will make your forehead like a diamond,{a} harder than flint rock. Do not fear them. Do not let their stares scare you. They are a rebel people.”
He went on, “Son of man, keep in your heart every word I tell you. Listen well.
Go to the exiles, your own people, and give them the message: ‘The Lord Yahweh says so.’ Do this whether they listen or refuse.”
Then the Spirit lifted me. Behind me came a loud rumbling: “Yahweh’s glory is to be praised in the place where He lives!”{b}
It was the sound of the creatures’ wings brushing against each other. It was also the wheels beside them, turning with a loud roar.
The Spirit raised me and took me away. I traveled with a bitter heart and a burning spirit, while Yahweh’s hand pressed down hard on me.
At Tel-abib{c} I found the exiles who lived beside the Chebar canal. Seven days went by while I sat among them, stunned.
When the seven days ended, a message from Yahweh came to me.
“Mortal one, I am putting you on watch over Israel. Whenever you hear a word from My mouth, pass it on to them as My warning.
Say I tell a wicked man, ‘You are going to die.’ If you stay quiet and do not warn him to leave his evil road, he will die in his sin. His blood, though, will be on your hands.
But if you warn him and he still will not leave his evil road, he will die in his sin. Your own life, however, will be safe.

Or say a good man turns from what is right and does evil. I may set a stumbling block in front of him, and he will die. If you gave no warning, he dies in his sin, and none of his earlier good deeds will count. His blood will be on your hands.
If instead you warn that good man to stop sinning, and he stops, he will live, because he listened. You will have rescued yourself as well.”
Yahweh’s hand rested on me there. “Get up,” He told me, “and walk out to the valley.{d} I will talk with you in that place.”
So off I went to the valley. Yahweh’s glory stood waiting there, as it had by the Chebar canal. I dropped to the ground, face down.
The Spirit came inside me and lifted me upright. Then He spoke: “Go home and lock yourself in.
Mortal one, they will tie you with ropes, and you will not be able to walk out among the people.
I will glue your tongue to the roof of your mouth. Not a word will come out, and you cannot scold them, for they rebel against Me.

Later, when I have something to say to you, I will unlock your lips. Then you will announce: ‘The Lord Yahweh says so.’ Those who choose to hear, will hear. Those who choose to refuse, will refuse. They are rebels.”

notes.text: The Hebrew word is shamir, a very hard stone. It may be emery or diamond.
With a small change in one Hebrew letter, the text could say, “as the glory of Yahweh rose up from the place where He lives.”
Tel-abib may mean “hill of new grain.” It was probably a Hebrew form of a Babylonian place name.
The Hebrew word can also mean “plain.”

verses.text: “Mortal one, get a clay brick and lay it in front of you. Sketch Jerusalem on it.
Then show the city under attack. Build a wall of siege towers and a ramp against it. Place army camps around it, and set battering rams on every side.

Next, find an iron cooking sheet and stand it between yourself and the city, like a wall of iron. Aim your face at the city. It is surrounded, and you are the one surrounding it. All this is a sign for Israel.
Now lie down on your left side. You will carry the guilt of Israel. You will carry it for as many days as you lie there.
I am giving you one day for each year of their guilt. That is 390 days.{a} In this way you will carry the guilt of Israel.
After you finish, roll over and lie on your right side. For forty days you will carry Judah’s guilt, one day standing for one year.
Turn your face toward Jerusalem under attack. Bare your arm, and speak against the city as a prophet.
I am putting ropes on you. You cannot turn from one side to the other until your days of attack are over.
Now take wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet, and spelt. Pour them into one jar, and make bread from them. You will eat this bread for all 390 days that you lie on your side.
Your food will be weighed. Eat about eight ounces{b} each day, at set times.
Water will be measured too: about two-thirds of a quart{c} a day, sipped at set times.
Bake your bread like a barley cake, and bake it in front of everyone over a fire of human waste.”
Yahweh said, “This is how Israel will eat their bread: unclean, among the nations where I will drive them.”

But I said, “Oh no, Lord Yahweh! I have never made myself unclean. From my youth until now, I have not eaten any animal that died on its own or was killed by wild beasts. Rotten meat has never entered my mouth.”
“Fine,” He said. “You may bake over cow dung and skip the human waste.”
He went on, “Mortal one, I will soon break Jerusalem’s supply of bread. They will weigh their bread and eat it in worry. They will measure their water and drink it in fear.
Bread and water will run short. People will stare at each other in terror, and they will waste away because of their guilt.”

notes.text: The Greek has “190 days” here and in verse 9, and “150 days” in verse 4. The Hebrew has 390.
The Hebrew says “twenty shekels.” That is about 230 grams.
The Hebrew says “a sixth of a hin.” That is about 0.6 liter.

verses.text: “Mortal one, pick up a sharp sword and treat it as a barber’s razor. Run it across your head and chin. Then weigh the cut hair on scales and split it into three piles.

When the days of the siege end, set one pile on fire inside the city. Chop the second pile with the sword around the city’s edge. Toss the last pile to the wind, and a drawn sword of Mine will go after it.
But pick out a few hairs and tie them in the edge of your robe.
Take a few of those again and throw them into the fire. A fire will spread from there to all of Israel.”
This is what the Lord Yahweh says: “I put Jerusalem in the middle of the nations, with lands all around her.
She has turned My laws into wicked acts, worse than the nations did. She has done the same with My rules, worse than the lands around her. She has thrown out My laws and has not lived by My rules.
So the Lord Yahweh says: Your trouble-making beats that of every nation near you. You ignored My rules and disobeyed My laws. You did not even match what the nations around you consider right.{a}
So the Lord Yahweh says: I Myself have turned against you. While the nations look on, I will punish you.
Because of all your hateful acts, I will do to you what I have never done and will never do again.

In your city, mothers and fathers will eat their sons and daughters, and grown children will eat their parents. I will carry out My punishments on you, and I will blow every survivor in all directions.
As surely as I live, says the Lord Yahweh, you filled My holy place with ugly idols and hateful acts, and so I will turn away.{b} I will not pity you or spare you.
One third of you will die of sickness or hunger inside your city. One third will fall by the sword outside it. I will scatter the last third to every wind and chase them with a drawn sword.
Then My anger will be finished. My fury against them will be satisfied, and I will be calm. When I have poured it all out, they will know that I, Yahweh, spoke out of My deep love for My own name.
I will make you a ruin and a joke to the nations around you, in the sight of everyone who walks by.
You will be shamed and laughed at. You will be a warning and a shock to the nations around you, when I punish you in anger and rage. I, Yahweh, have spoken.
I will shoot the arrows of hunger at you. They are arrows that destroy, and I will send them to destroy you. I will make the hunger worse and cut off your bread.
Hunger and wild animals will come from Me, and they will take your children. Disease and bloodshed will sweep past, and a sword from Me will fall on you. I, Yahweh, have spoken.”

notes.text: Some ancient copies leave out the word “not” here. They say, “but have lived by the standards of the nations around you.”
Or “I will cut you down.” The Hebrew verb is uncertain.

verses.text: A message from Yahweh came to me.
“Mortal one, face the mountains of Israel and prophesy against them.

Tell them: Mountains of Israel, hear what the Lord Yahweh says! He calls to the mountains and hills, to the creek beds and valleys. ‘I am bringing a sword against you. I will tear down your hilltop shrines.{a}
Your altars will be wrecked, and your incense stands will be smashed. Your dead will fall right before your idols.{b}
I will place Israel’s dead bodies before their idols. Around your altars I will spread their bones.

Wherever you live, towns will become ruins. Hilltop shrines will be torn down. Altars will be wrecked and left empty. Idols will be broken to pieces. Incense altars will be cut down, and all that your hands made will be wiped out.
Dead bodies will lie among you, and you will know that I am Yahweh.
‘Still, I will keep some of you alive. A few will get away from the sword and live among the nations, scattered across many lands.

Those who get away will think of Me while they are prisoners among the nations. They will remember how their unfaithful hearts broke My heart, and how their eyes chased after idols. They will be disgusted with themselves over the evil and hateful things they did.
They will learn that I am Yahweh. My threat to bring this disaster on them was not empty.’
“This is what the Lord Yahweh says: Clap your hands and stomp your foot. Cry out, ‘How awful!’ Look at all the hateful things Israel has done! They will fall by the sword, by hunger, and by disease.
Those far away will die of disease. Those nearby will fall to the sword. Those who survive that will die of hunger. In this way I will pour out all My anger on them.

You will know that I am Yahweh when their dead lie among the idols and around the altars. Bodies will lie on each high hill and mountaintop, under every green tree and thick oak, in the very places where they burned sweet incense to their idols.
My hand will stretch out against them. Their land will become a bare wasteland, from the desert to Diblah,{c} in every place they live. That is when they will learn that I am Yahweh.”

notes.text: Hilltop shrines were places for worship, often of other gods.
The Hebrew word for idols is gillulim, a word of contempt. It may mean “dung-gods.” It is used about forty times in Ezekiel.
No one knows where Diblah was. Many scholars read Riblah, a town in Syria, because the Hebrew letters for d and r look alike.

verses.text: A message from Yahweh came to me.
“Mortal one, this is what the Lord Yahweh says about the land of Israel.{a} The end! The end has come to all four corners of the land.
Now the end is on you. I will let My anger loose against you. I will judge you by the way you lived, and I will pay you back for all your hateful acts.
I will show no pity. I will charge you for how you lived, and your hateful acts will stay with you. Then you will know that I am Yahweh.
This is what the Lord Yahweh says: Disaster after disaster is on its way!
The end is here. The end is awake and rising against you. It is coming!
Your turn has come,{b} you who live in this land. The time is here. The day is close. On the mountains there will be panic, not happy shouts.
Soon I will pour out My rage on you and use up My anger against you. I will judge you by your ways and charge you for every hateful act.
I will show no pity. I will charge you for how you lived, and your hateful acts will stay with you. Then you will know that I, Yahweh, am the one who delivers the blow.
The day is here! It is coming! Your turn has come. Pride has grown into a rod, and it has flowered.
Violence has grown into a rod that punishes evil. Nothing will be left of the crowd, their wealth, or anything of value among them.{c}
The time has come. The day is here. The buyer should not cheer, and the seller should not cry, for anger burns against the whole crowd.
A seller will never return to what he sold, as long as both men live. The vision covers the whole crowd, and it will not be undone. Because of their sins, none will hold on to life.{d}
The trumpet has sounded and all is ready. Still, nobody goes out to fight, since My anger is on that whole crowd.
Swords wait outside. Disease and hunger wait inside. Whoever is in the fields will be killed by a sword. Whoever is in the city will be swallowed by hunger and disease.
Some will escape to the mountains, moaning like doves of the valleys, each one grieving over his own sin.
Every hand will go limp. Every knee will turn to water.{e}
They will put on sackcloth and shiver in terror. Shame will cover every face, and every head will be bald.

They will toss their silver on the streets, and gold will become garbage to them. On the day of Yahweh’s anger, neither can save them. Neither can satisfy their hunger or fill their stomachs, because they caused the fall into sin.
Their lovely jewelry made them proud. They shaped their hateful idols and ugly statues out of it. So I will turn it into garbage for them.
Foreigners will carry it off as loot. The earth’s wicked people will win it as a prize. They will make it unclean.
I will look away while they ruin My treasured place. Thieves will walk in and make it unclean.
Make chains,{f} because murder fills the land and violence fills the city.
I will bring the cruelest of the nations to take their homes. The pride of the strong will end, and their holy places will be ruined.
Terror will arrive! They will search for peace and find nothing.
Trouble will follow trouble, and rumor will follow rumor. They will beg a prophet for a vision. But the priest will have no teaching left, and the elders will have no advice.

The king will mourn, and the prince will dress in despair. The common people will tremble. I will treat them as their ways deserve, and I will judge them by their own judgments. That is when they will learn that I am Yahweh.”

notes.text: The Greek puts verses 3–9 in a different order and in a shorter form.
The Hebrew word is tsephirah, a word of uncertain meaning. It is also in verse 10. Others translate it “doom” or “crown.”
The Hebrew of verse 11 is hard to understand.
The Hebrew of verse 13 is hard. “Keep his life” may also mean “make himself strong.”
That is, they will wet themselves from fear.
The meaning of this phrase is uncertain, and the Greek leaves it out.

verses.text: On the fifth day of the sixth month (in August–September),{a} in the sixth year, the Judean leaders came to my house and sat down near me. There the hand of the Lord Yahweh landed on me.
I looked and saw a figure like a man made of fire.{b} Below His waist He looked like fire. Above His waist He glowed like shining metal.

He stretched out what seemed to be a hand and took hold of my hair. The Spirit lifted me up high between earth and sky. In visions from God, He carried me to Jerusalem. He set me at the entrance of the north gate of the inner courtyard, where a jealousy-making idol stood.
There too was the glory of Israel’s God, shining as it had in the vision from the valley.
God told me, “Mortal one, look north.” I looked, and there at the entrance north of the altar gate stood the idol that makes God jealous.
He asked, “Mortal one, do you see what they are doing? Israel does terrible, hateful things here that drive Me from My holy place. You will see even worse.”
He led me on to the courtyard gate, where I noticed a hole in the wall.
“Mortal one,” He said, “dig through the wall.” I dug, and I found a doorway.
He said, “Go in and look at the wicked, hateful things they are doing in there.”
Inside, I saw pictures cut into every wall: crawling creatures, unclean animals, and all the idols of Israel.
Seventy of Israel’s elders stood in front of the pictures. Jaazaniah,{c} son of Shaphan,{d} stood among them. Each man held a pan for burning incense, and a cloud of sweet smoke rose up.
God asked me, “Mortal one, do you see what Israel’s elders do in the dark? Each man does it in his own room full of carved idols. They say, ‘Yahweh cannot see us. Yahweh has left the land.’”
He added, “You will see them do even worse things.”
Next He brought me to the north entrance of Yahweh’s house. Women were sitting there, crying over the god Tammuz.{e}
He said, “Mortal one, did you see that? You will see worse things than these.”

Then He took me into the inner courtyard of Yahweh’s house. Between the porch and the altar, at the door of Yahweh’s temple, stood about twenty-five men. Their backs were to the temple of Yahweh, and they faced east. They were bowing to the rising sun.

He said, “Mortal one, do you see this? Is it too small a thing for Judah to do these hateful acts here? They also fill the land with violence and keep making Me angry. They even hold a branch to their noses!{f}
So I will answer in fury. I will not pity them or spare them. They may shout in My ears, but I will not listen.”

notes.text: The Hebrew says “in the sixth year, in the sixth month, on the fifth day of the month.” Months are counted from spring.
The Hebrew says “fire.” The Greek says “a man,” which many scholars prefer. Compare 1:27.
Jaazaniah means “Yahweh listens.”
Shaphan means “rock badger.” He was probably the king’s secretary in the time of Josiah.
Tammuz was a god of Mesopotamia. People mourned his death each summer.
No one is sure what this means. It may describe a ritual gesture for a false god, or an insult.

verses.text: God shouted so I could hear: “Bring the city’s punishers here, each with his weapon of ruin in hand!”

Six men arrived from the direction of the upper north gate. Each one carried a smashing weapon. With them came one more man, dressed in linen, with a writer’s kit hanging at his side. All of them walked in and halted next to the bronze altar.
Up from the winged guardian{a} where it had rested rose the glory of Israel’s God, and it moved to the temple’s threshold. Yahweh then called to the man in linen with the writer’s kit.
Yahweh told him, “Go through Jerusalem, all of it. Draw a mark{b} on the forehead of each person who sighs and cries over the hateful things done there.”
Then I heard Him tell the other men, “Follow him through the city and strike. Do not pity anyone. Do not hold back.

Kill old men, young men, girls, children, and women, until they are all gone. Anyone wearing the mark, you must not touch. My own holy place is where you start.” The elders in front of the temple were the first to fall.
He told them, “Make the temple unclean. Fill its courtyards with the dead. Go!” They went out and struck down people all over the city.
While they were killing, I was left alone. I threw myself face down and shouted, “Oh no, Lord Yahweh! As You pour out Your anger on Jerusalem, will You wipe out all who remain in Israel?”
He replied, “The sin of Israel and Judah is huge. Murder fills the land, and unfairness fills the city. They say, ‘Yahweh has left the land. Yahweh does not see.’
So I will give them no pity and no mercy. I will make them pay for what they have done.”
The man in linen, the writer’s kit at his side, then returned with his report: “I did exactly what You told me.”

notes.text: Cherubim were winged beings that guarded holy places. See Genesis 3:24. These are probably the cherubim over the ark in the Most Holy Place.
The Hebrew word is taw, the last letter of the Hebrew alphabet. In the writing of that time it looked like an X or a cross.

verses.text: I looked at the dome over the cherubim’s heads. Above it was something that looked like a throne of deep blue stone.

God spoke to the man in linen: “Step between the spinning wheels{a} under the cherubim. Fill both of your hands with burning coals from among the cherubim, and scatter them over the city.” I watched him step in.
When the man went in, the cherubim were standing on the south side of the temple, and a cloud filled the inner courtyard.
Yahweh’s glory rose from the cherub and moved to the temple’s threshold. The cloud filled the temple, and the bright light of Yahweh’s glory filled the courtyard.
The sound of the cherubim’s wings reached all the way to the outer courtyard. It sounded like El Shaddai{b} speaking.
God ordered the man in linen, “Take fire from between the spinning wheels, from among the cherubim.” The man entered and took his place beside a wheel.
One cherub stretched out a hand to the fire between them, scooped some up, and put it in the linen man’s hands. The man took it and went out.
Under the cherubim’s wings I could see what looked like human hands.
Then I saw four wheels beside the cherubim, one next to each cherub. They sparkled like a golden-green gem.
All four wheels looked the same, as if one wheel crossed through the middle of another.
They could roll in any of the four directions. They did not need to turn. They went in the direction the front of the creature faced, and they never turned as they went.
Eyes covered the cherubim’s entire bodies, including their backs, hands, and wings. The wheels were full of eyes all the way around, too, all four of them.
I heard someone call the wheels “spinning wheels.”{c}
Each cherub had four faces. One was a cherub’s face. The next was a man’s. The third was a lion’s. The last was an eagle’s.{d}
The cherubim then lifted up. Here were the very beings I had seen beside the Chebar canal.
Whenever a cherub moved, a wheel moved at its side. Whenever one opened its wings to leave the ground, the wheels never left it.
If a cherub halted, so did the wheels. If a cherub rose, the wheels rose with it, since the creature’s spirit lived in them.
Then Yahweh’s glory left the temple’s threshold and stopped over the cherubim.
As I watched, the cherubim opened their wings and left the ground, and the wheels went up with them. At the east gate of Yahweh’s house they stopped, and the glory of Israel’s God hovered above.
These were the creatures I had seen under Israel’s God by the Chebar canal. Now I knew they were cherubim.
Each had four faces and four wings, with something like human hands under the wings.
Their faces matched the faces I had seen by the Chebar canal. Each went straight ahead.

notes.text: The Hebrew word is galgal. It is also in verses 6 and 13.
El Shaddai is often translated “God Almighty.” The first meaning of Shaddai is uncertain.
The Hebrew word galgal suggests something that whirls or rolls.
Verse 14 is not found in the Greek. Compare 1:10, where an ox’s face takes the place of “the face of a cherub.”

verses.text: The Spirit lifted me and set me down at the east gate of Yahweh’s house. Twenty-five men stood at its entrance. Among them I saw two leaders of the people: Jaazaniah son of Azzur{a} and Pelatiah{b} son of Benaiah.{c}
God told me, “Mortal one, these are the men who make wicked plans and give harmful advice in this city.
They say, ‘Building homes will happen soon. Think of this city as a kettle and ourselves as the choice meat inside.’{d}
So speak against them. Prophesy, mortal one.”
Then the Spirit of Yahweh came on me, and He said, “Give them this message from Yahweh. People of Israel, I know what you have said and what goes on in your minds.
Many have died by your hands in this city. Its streets are piled with your victims.
So the Lord Yahweh says this: The dead you piled up inside the city are the meat, and the city is the pot. But I am going to drag you out of it.
You were afraid of the sword, so I will bring the sword against you, says the Lord Yahweh.
Out of the city I will haul you, and strangers will get you. I will carry out My punishments on you.
You will fall by the sword. At the edge of Israel’s land I will pass sentence on you. Then you will learn that I am Yahweh.
No, this city will not be your kettle, and you will not be the meat in it. Out at Israel’s border I will pass sentence on you.
You will learn that I am Yahweh. You did not follow My rules or keep My laws. You copied the nations around you instead.”{e}
While I was still speaking God’s message, Pelatiah son of Benaiah dropped dead. I fell on my face and cried out loudly, “Oh no, Lord Yahweh! Are You going to finish off everyone left in Israel?”
A message from Yahweh came to me.
“Mortal one, think of your brothers, your relatives,{f} and all the exiles of Israel. The people of Jerusalem say about them, ‘They are far from Yahweh. This land was given to us to own.’

So give them this answer from the Lord Yahweh: It is true that I sent them far away among the nations and scattered them through the lands. Yet I have been a little holy place{g} for them in the lands where they went.
Give them this answer too from the Lord Yahweh: From the nations I will round you up. From the lands where you were scattered I will bring you home. The land of Israel will be yours.
When they return, they will clear out every ugly idol and hateful thing.
I will give them one heart{h} and a new spirit within. The heart of stone I will take away, and a soft, living heart will take its place.
After that, My rules will guide their steps, and they will respect My laws. They will be My people, and I will be their God.
But some people long for ugly idols and hateful things. I will make them pay for what they do, says the Lord Yahweh.”
Then the cherubim opened their wings, with the wheels at their sides. The glory of Israel’s God rose above them.
Yahweh’s glory went up and away from the city, and rested on the mountain to its east.{i}
The Spirit lifted me up in the vision, by the Spirit of God, and took me to the exiles in Chaldea. Then the vision faded.
I told the exiles everything Yahweh had shown me.

notes.text: Azzur means “helper.” This Jaazaniah is not the man in 8:11.
Pelatiah means “Yahweh rescues.” This gives meaning to the cry in verse 13.
Benaiah means “Yahweh has built.”
The Hebrew can also mean, “It is not time to build houses.” The pot picture shows that the leaders thought they were the best meat, safe inside the city.
Verses 11–12 are not found in the Greek.
The Hebrew says “the men of your redemption.” These were relatives with the duty to buy back family land. See Leviticus 25:25. The Greek has “the men of your captivity.”
Or “a holy place for a little while.”
Some Hebrew copies and the Greek have “another heart.” Others read “a heart not divided.”
This is the Mount of Olives.

verses.text: A message from Yahweh came to me.
“Mortal one, you live among rebels. Their eyes work, yet nothing registers. Their ears work, yet nothing sinks in. That is because they are rebels.
So prepare a bag as if you were being sent into exile. In broad daylight, with the people watching, leave your home for another place. They may catch on, although they are rebels.
In the daytime, carry out your bag in front of them, like an exile’s bag. Then in the evening, go out yourself in front of them, like someone being taken away.
With everyone looking on, break a hole in the wall and pass your things through it.
As they watch, hoist the bag to your shoulder and leave in the dark. Cover your face to keep the land out of sight. You are My warning sign to the house of Israel.”

I did exactly as I was told. In the daytime I carried my bag out, like an exile’s bag. In the evening I dug through the wall with my hands. In the dark I lifted the bag onto my shoulder and carried it out while they watched.
The next morning, a message from Yahweh came to me.
“Mortal one, did the rebel people of Israel ask you, ‘What are you doing?’
Tell them what the Lord Yahweh says: This message{a} concerns the prince in Jerusalem and every Israelite living in that city.
Tell them, ‘I am a sign for you. Whatever I did, they will go through. Prisoners, hauled off to exile.’
The prince among them will shoulder his bag at dusk and slip out. A gap will be broken in the wall for his escape. His own face will be covered, so the land stays hidden from his eyes.
My net will fall over him, and My trap will close. I will bring him to Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans. His eyes will never see that land, and there he will die.{b}
All who surround him, his helpers and his armies, I will scatter to every wind. I will chase them with a drawn sword.
They will know that I am Yahweh once I spread them among the nations and sow them across the lands.

Yet a few I will keep alive through sword, hunger, and disease. Wherever they end up among the nations, they will confess all the hateful things they did. That is when they will know that I am Yahweh.”
A message from Yahweh came to me.
“Mortal one, eat your bread while you shake. Drink your water while you tremble and worry.

Then tell the people of the land that the Lord Yahweh says this about those living in Jerusalem, in Israel’s land: They will eat bread in fear and drink water in terror. Everything in their land will be taken away, since all its people have been so violent.
Towns where people live will be ruined, and the land will become a desert. Then you will know that I am Yahweh.”
A message from Yahweh came to me.
“Mortal one, what is this proverb you repeat in Israel’s land? You say, ‘Time drags on, and no vision comes true.’
Tell them that the Lord Yahweh says: I will stop that proverb. Nobody in Israel will repeat it again. Say this instead: ‘The days are close. Every vision is about to happen.
There will be no more false visions, and no more smooth lies from fortune-tellers in Israel.
I am Yahweh. When I speak, My word will happen, and it will not be put off. In your own days, you rebels, I will speak and I will do it, says the Lord Yahweh.’”
A message from Yahweh came to me.
“Mortal one, the people of Israel are saying, ‘The vision he sees is for a time far off. He prophesies about the distant future.’
So tell them that the Lord Yahweh says: No more waiting for any of My words. Whatever I say will happen, says the Lord Yahweh.”

notes.text: The Hebrew word is massa, which can mean “burden” or “message.” It plays on the bag that was carried, and on the word for prince, nasi, which means “one lifted up.”
King Zedekiah was blinded before he was taken to Babylon. See 2 Kings 25:7.

verses.text: A message from Yahweh came to me.
“Mortal one, speak against the prophets of Israel who make up messages from their own minds. Tell them to hear the word of Yahweh.
This is what the Lord Yahweh says: How terrible for foolish prophets! They follow their own spirit and have seen nothing.
Israel, your prophets are like wild dogs in a pile of ruins.
You never went up to the cracks in the wall. You never fixed the wall for Israel, so it could stand in the fight on the day of Yahweh.
What they see is false, and their fortune-telling is a lie. They say, ‘Yahweh says,’ when Yahweh did not send them. Still they wait for their words to come true.
You saw a false vision and told a lying fortune. You said, ‘Yahweh says,’ but I never spoke.
So the Lord Yahweh says: You have spoken lies and seen false things. Now I am against you, says the Lord Yahweh.

My hand will come down on prophets whose visions are false and whose fortunes are lies. They will have no seat in My people’s council. No record of Israel will carry their names. Their feet will never enter Israel’s land. Then you will know that I am the Lord Yahweh.
They have pulled My people off the path. They cry, ‘Peace,’ when there is no peace. Someone builds a flimsy wall, and they paint it with whitewash.
Tell those whitewashers that the wall will fall. A flooding rain will come. Great hailstones will drop, and a stormy wind will break loose.
When the wall falls, people will ask you, ‘Where is the whitewash you put on it?’
So the Lord Yahweh says: In My anger I will send a storm wind. In My rage there will be flooding rain and hailstones that destroy.
I will knock down the wall you covered with whitewash. I will flatten it, and its base will show. When it falls, you will die under it. Then you will know that I am Yahweh.
I will finish My anger on the wall and on those who whitewashed it. Then I will say to you, ‘The wall is gone, and so are those who covered it.
These were the prophets of Israel who spoke to Jerusalem. They saw visions of peace for her, though no peace existed,’ says the Lord Yahweh.”
“Mortal one, now speak against the women among your people who prophesy from their own minds.

Tell them what the Lord Yahweh says: Shame on you women who tie magic bands{a} around every wrist and make veils to fit heads of all sizes, so you can hunt souls! Do you think you can hunt down the lives of My people and still keep yours safe?

For a few handfuls of barley and some crumbs of bread, you have brought shame on Me among My people. By your lies you have put to death some who should not die, and spared some who should not live. My people were happy to hear lies.
So the Lord Yahweh says: I will fight your magic bands, the traps you use to catch people like birds. I will rip them from your arms and let your captives fly free.
Your veils I will tear away, and out of your grasp I will pull My people. They will never be your prey again. Then you will know that I am Yahweh.
With lies you made honest people sad, though I had not hurt them. You cheered up the wicked, so they never turned from evil to save themselves.
That is why your false visions and fortune-telling will end. I will pull My people free from your grip, and you will know that I am Yahweh.”

notes.text: No one is sure what the Hebrew words for “bands” and “veils” mean. They were probably objects used for magic.

verses.text: Some of Israel’s elders came and sat down in front of me.
Yahweh spoke to me again.
“Mortal one, these men have let idols settle in their hearts. They keep their sin right in front of them, ready to trip them. Why should I let them ask Me anything?

So speak to them. Tell them, ‘The Lord Yahweh says: Any Israelite who holds idols in his heart and keeps his sin before his eyes, and then comes to a prophet, will get his answer from Me. I, Yahweh, will answer him myself, and the answer will fit his pile of idols.
I will do this to win back the hearts of Israel’s people, for every one of them has drifted away from Me through his idols.’
“So tell the people of Israel, ‘The Lord Yahweh says: Turn back! Leave your idols, and turn from every one of your vile habits.

Any Israelite, or any foreigner living with Israel, who pulls away from Me and holds idols in his heart, and who keeps his sin before his eyes and then comes to a prophet to ask Me a question, will get his answer from Me. I, Yahweh, will answer him Myself.
I will turn against that man. I will make him a warning that people repeat as a saying. I will remove him from My people, and you will know that I am Yahweh.
“‘And if a prophet is fooled into giving an answer, it is I, Yahweh, who allowed that prophet to be fooled. I will raise My hand against him and destroy him from among My people Israel.
Both will carry their guilt. The prophet and the man who asked him will be equally guilty.
Then Israel will stop wandering away from Me. They will stop making themselves unclean with their sins. They will be My people, and I will be their God, says the Lord Yahweh.’”
Another message from Yahweh came to me.
“Mortal one, suppose a country sins against Me by turning from Me. I reach out My hand against it. I cut off its food supply and send hunger, so that people and animals die.
Even if Noah, Daniel,{a} and Job lived there, their goodness would save only themselves, says the Lord Yahweh.
“Or suppose wild animals roam that country. They leave it without children, and the land becomes so empty that nobody dares cross it, for fear of the beasts.
I swear by My own life, says the Lord Yahweh, that those three men could not save even their own sons or daughters if they were there. Only they would be rescued, and the land would be a wasteland.
“Or suppose war comes to that country at My command. ‘Let swords sweep across it!’ I say, and people and animals are cut down.
I swear by My own life, says the Lord Yahweh, that those three men could not rescue sons or daughters there. Only they would be rescued.
“Or suppose I send a deadly sickness into that country and pour out My anger in blood, so that people and animals die.
As surely as I live, says the Lord Yahweh, Noah, Daniel, and Job could not save a son or a daughter. Their goodness would save only themselves.”

This is what the Lord Yahweh says: It will be far worse when I send all four of My terrible punishments against Jerusalem: war, hunger, wild animals, and sickness. They will destroy people and animals alike.

Yet some survivors will be left there, sons and daughters who are led out. They will come to you, and you will see how they have lived and what they have done. Then you will be comforted about the disaster I brought on Jerusalem, about everything I did to it.
You will find comfort when you see their lives and actions. You will know that I did nothing to Jerusalem without a reason, says the Lord Yahweh.

notes.text: The Hebrew spelling is Danel (as also in 28:3). He was a righteous hero of ancient times, known from texts found at Ugarit. Jewish tradition connects him with the Daniel of the book of Daniel. The name means “God is my judge.”

verses.text: Yahweh spoke to me again.
“Mortal one, is a grapevine’s wood worth more than the wood of any other tree in the forest?
Can anyone make something useful from it? Could you carve even a peg from it to hang a tool on?
No. People toss it on the fire as fuel. The flames burn both ends, and the middle turns black. Is it good for anything then?
It was useless even when whole. Once flames have eaten it and left it scorched, surely nothing can be made from it!
So the Lord Yahweh says: I gave the vine’s wood to the fire as fuel. It was only one kind of tree among all the trees of the forest. I will do the same to the people of Jerusalem.
I will turn against them. They got out of one fire, but another fire will burn them up. Then, when My anger falls on them, you will know that I am Yahweh.
I will make the land empty, because the people turned away from Me, says the Lord Yahweh.”
Yahweh spoke to me again.
“Mortal one, make Jerusalem face her disgusting deeds.
Tell her, ‘The Lord Yahweh says to Jerusalem: Canaan is where you began and where you were born. A man from the Amorites fathered you, and a Hittite woman gave you birth.{a}
When your birth day came, no one cut the cord, washed you, rubbed you with salt, or wrapped you in cloths.
Nobody felt sorry enough to do any of this for you. You were unwanted, so someone threw you out into an open field right after you were born.
“‘I walked past and saw you kicking in your blood. Lying there in that blood, you heard Me command, “Live!” Yes, “Live!” was My word to you in that bloody place.{b}
I caused you to grow as a field plant grows. You became tall and very lovely.{c} You reached young womanhood, yet you were completely bare.

“‘Later I walked by again and saw that the time for love had come for you. I laid the edge of My robe over you and covered your body. I made a solemn promise and entered a covenant with you, says the Lord Yahweh, and you became Mine.
I washed the blood from you with water and rubbed oil on your skin.
I dressed you in colorful cloth and gave you sandals of fine leather.{d} I wrapped you in linen and covered you with silk.
Then I gave you jewelry: bracelets for your wrists and a necklace.
A jewel hung from your nose, rings from your ears, and a lovely crown rested on your head.
You wore gold and silver. Your clothes were linen, silk, and colorful cloth. Your food was the finest flour, along with honey and olive oil. You became very beautiful, and you ruled as a queen.
The nations heard of you because of your beauty. It was flawless, for I had put My own glory on you, declares the Lord Yahweh.
“‘Yet you trusted in your own beauty. You used your fame to give yourself to other gods. You offered yourself to every person who walked by, and your beauty belonged to him.{e}
You took some of your clothes and made bright little shrines. There you gave yourself to other gods. Such things should never happen.
You took the beautiful jewelry that I had given you, made of My gold and silver. You made statues of men from it and gave yourself to them.
You put your colorful clothes on them. My oil and My incense were what you laid before them.
I had given you food: the best flour, olive oil, and honey. You put it before those statues as a sweet smell. That is what you did, says the Lord Yahweh.
“‘You took the sons and daughters you had borne for Me and killed them as food for those statues. Was your unfaithfulness not bad enough already?
You killed My children and handed them over, making them pass through fire for those statues.
In all your disgusting deeds and unfaithfulness, you never remembered your young days, when you lay bare and kicking in your blood.
“‘After all this evil you did (how sad for you, says the Lord Yahweh!), you set up a platform and a high place in every public square.
You raised up your own mound there. Every public square had a high place of yours.
At the head of every street you built a high place. You made your beauty something disgusting. You offered yourself to everyone who passed by, again and again.
You gave yourself to the Egyptians, your neighbors with strong desires.{f} You did it again and again to make Me angry.
So I reached out My hand against you and made your land smaller. I gave you up to the Philistine women, who hate you. Even they were shocked at your shameful ways.
You were never satisfied, so you gave yourself to the Assyrians too. Yet even with them you were left wanting more.
You went on to give yourself to Babylonia, the land of traders.{g} Even then you were not satisfied.
“‘Your heart is so weak and burning,{h} says the Lord Yahweh, when you do all these things like a bold and shameless woman.
At the head of every street you built your platform, and in every square you made your high place. But you were not like other such women, because you refused to be paid.
You are a wife who cheats! You welcome strangers in place of your husband.
Other women receive gifts, but you were the one who gave gifts to every lover. You paid them to come to you from all around.
You are the opposite of other women. Nobody chased you. You paid, and nobody paid you. You were the opposite.
“‘So hear the word of Yahweh, unfaithful city.
The Lord Yahweh says: You poured out your desire,{i} and you showed your bare body to your lovers. You did it with your idols, and you gave them the blood of your children.

So now I will call together all your lovers, the ones you enjoyed, whether you loved them or hated them. They will come from every direction to stand against you. I will take off your clothes before them, and they will look at you, completely bare.
I will judge you as the law judges women who cheat on their husbands or shed blood. I will bring on you the anger and jealous fury of blood.
I will hand you over to them. They will pull down your platform and smash your high places. They will strip off your clothes and take your fine jewelry, leaving you with nothing on.
A mob will come against you. Its people will stone you and hack you to pieces with swords.
They will burn down your houses and punish you while many women watch. I will stop your unfaithfulness, and you will never pay lovers again.
Then My anger against you will cool. My jealousy will leave you. I will be calm and no longer angry.

You did not remember your young days. You made Me furious with all this. So now I will make you pay for what you did, says the Lord Yahweh. Did you not add this shameful act to all your other disgusting deeds?
“‘Look, everyone who loves sayings will say about you: “Like mother, like daughter.”

You are truly your mother’s daughter, for she hated her husband and her children. Your sisters hated their husbands and children too, and you are like them. Your mother came from the Hittites, and your father from the Amorites.
Your older sister is Samaria. She and her daughters lived on your north side.{j} Your younger sister is Sodom. She and her daughters lived on your south side.
It was not enough for you to walk in their ways and copy their disgusting deeds. Very soon you were acting even worse than they did.
As surely as I live, says the Lord Yahweh, your sister Sodom and her daughters never did anything like what you and your daughters have done.
Here is the guilt of your sister Sodom: She and her daughters were proud. Food was plentiful and life was easy, but they never helped the poor and needy.
They became arrogant and did disgusting things before Me. So I took them away, as you have seen.{k}
Samaria’s sins were not even half of yours. You have done more disgusting things than she did. Next to all your deeds, your sisters look good.

Now you must carry your shame, for you spoke up for your sisters. Your sins were so much worse than theirs that they look better than you. So be ashamed and carry your shame, for you made your sisters look good.
“‘Yet I will bring them back from captivity: Sodom with her daughters, Samaria with her daughters, and you with them.
Then you will carry your shame and be embarrassed by all you did. In this you will comfort them.
Sodom and Samaria, with their daughters, will be restored to what they once were. Your own turn will come as well, you and your daughters.
In your proud days you would not even speak your sister Sodom’s name.
That was before your evil was uncovered. Now you are like her. The daughters of Edom{l} and all the people around her look down on you, as do the Philistine women and everyone around you.
You must carry the weight of your shameful deeds and disgusting acts, says Yahweh.
“‘The Lord Yahweh says: I will repay you for your own actions. You looked down on your promise and broke the covenant.
Still, I will remember the covenant I made in your early days. I will set up a covenant with you that lasts forever, and then you will remember your ways.
Then you will remember your ways and be ashamed when you receive your sisters, both older and younger. I will give them to you as daughters, though not as part of your covenant.
I Myself will set up My covenant with you, and you will know that I am Yahweh.
You will remember and be ashamed. You will be too embarrassed to open your mouth, when I forgive you for everything you did, says the Lord Yahweh.’”

notes.text: The Amorites and Hittites were among the peoples living in Canaan before Israel. The point is that Jerusalem’s beginnings were not Israelite.
The Greek does not have the second “Live!”
The Hebrew is uncertain here. It may mean “you came to have the finest jewels.”
The Hebrew word is tahash, a fine leather. We do not know what animal it came from.
The Hebrew words “your beauty belonged to him” are uncertain.
Hebrew: “great of flesh,” a plain way of speaking of strong desire.
Hebrew: “the land of Canaan, Chaldea.” Here “Canaan” means “traders.”
Or “weak.” The Hebrew word is uncertain.
The Hebrew word is nechosheth, which may mean “copper” (that is, money) or “desire.” It is uncertain.
Hebrew: “on your left.” Facing east, the left side is north.
Or “as you saw.”
Some ancient copies say “Edom.” The Hebrew text and the Greek say “Aram” (Syria). The two names differ by one similar letter.

verses.text: I received another word from Yahweh.
“Mortal one, put a riddle before Israel’s family, and tell them a story with a hidden meaning.

Tell them, ‘The Lord Yahweh says this:
A huge eagle, with wide wings and long flight feathers,
its coat bright with many colors,
flew to Lebanon and seized the crown of a cedar.

He snapped off the highest young shoot
and took it to a land where people buy and sell.
There, in a traders’ city, he set it in the ground.

It sprang up and became a vine that spread out, but stayed short.
Its branches bent toward that eagle,
and its roots stayed under him.
So it grew into a vine, put out limbs, and sent up new shoots.

“‘After that, a second huge eagle arrived,
with wide wings and thick feathers.
Watch: this vine turned its roots toward him.
It stretched its thin stems his way,
leaving the bed where it had been set,
hoping he would water it.

Yet that vine already stood in good earth beside plenty of water,
able to grow limbs, grow fruit,
and become a splendid vine.’

“Now tell them, ‘The Lord Yahweh asks this: Can that vine do well? Will its roots not be yanked free and its fruit torn off, until every fresh leaf withers? You will not need a strong arm or a big crowd to pull it up, roots and all.
See, it has been planted a second time. Can it do well? When the wind from the east hits it, will it not wither completely—wither right in the bed where it first grew?’”
Yahweh spoke to me once more.

“Speak to this stubborn family. Ask them, ‘Do you not understand this story?’ Then explain: ‘The king of Babylon marched into Jerusalem. He seized its king and its leaders and took them home with him to Babylon.{b}
From the royal family he picked one man{c} and made a binding promise with him, sealing it with a solemn curse. The strong men of the land he also took away,
so the kingdom would stay weak and would not rise up. It would live on only by keeping that promise.
But that new king rebelled. Riders went from him to Egypt, asking for horses and a large army. Can he succeed? Can a man who acts this way go free? He broke the promise. Will he go free?

“‘I swear by My own life, says the Lord Yahweh: Babylon is where he will die—right in the city of the ruler who gave him the crown. That is the ruler whose solemn curse he treated as nothing and whose promise he broke.
Pharaoh may bring a huge army and a great force, but he will not help that king in the fight, once dirt ramps are piled up and siege towers are built to take many lives.
He treated the oath with contempt when he broke the promise. He had given his hand as a pledge, then did all this anyway. He will not get away.
“‘So the Lord Yahweh says: I swear by My own life—that solemn curse of Mine that he treated as nothing, and My promise that he broke, I will make him pay for both.
My net will drop over him, and My snare will hold him fast. Once he is in Babylon, I will try him there for the way he betrayed Me.
His best soldiers{d} in every group will die in battle, and anyone left alive will be scattered on every wind. That is how you will know Yahweh is the One who spoke.’

“The Lord Yahweh also says this:
I Myself will break a small branch from the high crown of the cedar and set it in the ground.
From the very top of its young growth I will take a tender shoot
and, with My own hand, set that shoot on a mountain that stands very high.

Israel’s high mountain is where I will set it.
Limbs will spread from it, fruit will grow on it,
and it will stand as a great cedar.
Winged creatures of every kind will make their home beneath it,
resting in the shadow of its limbs.

Then every tree in the field will understand
that I, Yahweh, pull the tall tree down
and lift the short tree up.
A green tree I can wither,
and a withered tree I can make thrive.
I, Yahweh, have spoken, and I will carry it out.”

notes.text: The Hebrew word rendered as a stream-side tree is uncertain.
This was when Nebuchadnezzar took King Jehoiachin away in 597 BC. See 2 Kings 24:10-17.
That man was Zedekiah. See 2 Kings 24:17.
Some ancient copies say “best soldiers.” The main Hebrew text says “fugitives.”

verses.text: Another message from Yahweh came to me.

“Why do you keep repeating this old line about the land of Israel:
‘Parents eat grapes that are still green,
but it is the children’s teeth that tingle’?
I swear by My own life, says the Lord Yahweh, you will stop using that saying in Israel.
Listen: every life belongs to Me. The father’s life is Mine, and the child’s life is Mine too. Death comes to the person who sins, not to someone else.
“Picture a man who does what is right. He treats people fairly and lives the right way.

Hill shrine meals are not for him. He will not lift his eyes toward the idols of Israel’s family. Another man’s wife is not someone he touches, and he keeps his distance from a woman during her monthly bleeding.

He cheats nobody. If he took a person’s coat as a promise to pay a debt, he gives it back. He does not steal. Hungry people receive food from him, and people with no clothes receive something to wear.
Interest is not what he charges when he lends, and he takes no extra fee. He refuses to do wrong, and when two people argue, he judges them fairly.
He follows My rules and carefully keeps My decisions. A man like that is in the right. He will live, says the Lord Yahweh.
“Now imagine that this same man fathers a son, a robber, a man who spills blood, and who does any of the things on this list—
things his father never did. This son eats at the hill shrines and sleeps with another man’s wife.
He crushes the poor and the needy. He steals. He keeps the coat that was left as a promise. He looks up to idols and does things I hate.
He lends for interest and charges a fee on top. Can a son like that live? He cannot. All these disgusting acts are his, and death will be his end. The blame for that death rests on him alone.
“But suppose that wicked man also has a son. This son sees every sin his father committed. He sees them and refuses to copy them.
Meals at the hill shrines are not for him. Israel’s family idols do not catch his eye. Another man’s wife is not someone he touches.
He cheats nobody. He does not keep a coat taken as a promise, and he does not steal. Hungry people receive food from him, and he covers anyone who lacks clothing.
The poor he refuses to harm.{a} He takes no interest and no extra fee. He follows My decisions and walks in My rules. His father’s guilt will not cause his death. He will live.
As for his father—that man squeezed people for money, robbed a fellow Israelite, and did what was evil among his own people. He will die for his own guilt.
“Still you ask, ‘Why does the son not pay for what his father did?’ If that son has practiced fairness and honesty, kept all My rules, and lived by them, life will be his.

It is the sinner who must die. A child will not bear a father’s guilt, and a father will not bear a child’s guilt. Each good person keeps the credit of his own right living, and each wicked person keeps the blame of his own evil.
“But if a wicked person leaves behind every sin of his past, keeps all My rules, and begins to live with fairness and honesty, life will be his. Death will not be.
None of the wrongs he once committed will be held against him. Because of the right things he now does, he will live.
Do I enjoy it when a wicked person dies? asks the Lord Yahweh. Would I not far rather see him turn from his path and live?

“But if a person who has been doing right walks away from it and starts doing wrong—the same hateful acts that wicked people do—can he live? The good he once did will not be added up in his favor. The betrayal he committed and the sins he did will be why he dies.
“Yet you say, ‘The Lord’s path does not measure up.’ Listen, family of Israel: Is My path the crooked one? Or do your own paths fall short?
When a person who has been doing right leaves that path and does wrong, he will die for it. The wrong he has done is why he dies.
And when a wicked person walks away from the evil he once did and starts living with fairness and honesty, that turn will keep him alive.
He took a hard look at his life, left behind every sin he had done, and so life will be his. Death will not be.
Still Israel’s family says, ‘The Lord’s path is not just.’ Family of Israel, is the problem in My path? The unfairness sits in your paths, not Mine.
“So I will judge you, family of Israel, each of you by how you have lived, says the Lord Yahweh. Turn around. Leave all the sins you have done, so that guilt will not bring you down.
Cast aside every rebellious act that has been yours, and let your heart be made new, and your spirit too. Family of Israel, why should you die?
I take no pleasure in anyone’s death, says the Lord Yahweh. So turn around, and live!”

notes.text: The main Hebrew text says “from the poor.” The Greek says “from injustice.” Compare verse 8.

verses.text: “Now you, lift up a funeral song for Israel’s princes,

and say:
‘Your mother was a lioness among the lions!
She rested among the young males
and raised her cubs there.

One cub she raised until he grew strong
and took his place as a young lion.
Tearing prey became what he knew,
and people were what he ate.

Word of him reached other nations.
Their pit became his trap.
With hooks they marched him off
into Egypt.{a}

“‘Once she realized hope was gone,
and that waiting had produced nothing,
she chose another of her cubs
and trained him as a young lion.

Among the lions he moved,
a young lion in his own right.
Tearing prey became what he knew,
and people were what he ate.

He attacked their strong places{b}
and wrecked their towns.
Everything in the land trembled
when his roar rang out.

Around him, nation after nation
rose from their territories.
A net was thrown across his path,
and their pit held him fast.

Hooks went into him, and a cage closed around him,
and off he was sent to Babylon’s king.{c}
Inside a fortress they held him,
so that his roar would never again be heard
among Israel’s hills.

“‘Your mother was also like a vine in your vineyard,{d}
set in the ground beside the water.
She grew fruit and many branches
because the water was plentiful.

Her branches were strong,
strong enough to be a king’s staff.
She rose high
above the thick leaves.
Everyone could see how tall she was
and how many limbs she had.

But in anger she was pulled up
and thrown on the ground.
The wind from the east dried her fruit.
Her strong limbs snapped off and withered,
and fire burned them up.

Now her place is a desert planting,
in ground that is dry and thirsty.

Fire has come out from her main stem.
It has burned up her shoots and her fruit.
No strong branch is left,
no staff for a king to hold.’
This song is a lament, and a lament is how it is used.”

notes.text: This was King Jehoahaz. Pharaoh Neco took him to Egypt in 609 BC. See 2 Kings 23:31-34.
The Hebrew says “He knew his widows.” A small change in the letters can mean “he tore down their strong places” or “he harmed their widows.”
This may be King Jehoiachin (2 Kings 24:8-15) or King Zedekiah (2 Kings 25:7).
The Hebrew says “in your blood.” The wording is unclear. Many readers think it first said “in a vineyard.”

verses.text: In the seventh year, on day ten of the fifth month (July–August),{a} a group of Israel’s elders came to ask Yahweh for guidance, and sat down facing me.
Yahweh spoke to me again.
“Mortal one, talk to Israel’s elders. Tell them, ‘The Lord Yahweh says: Did you come to ask Me for guidance? I swear by My own life that I will not answer you, says the Lord Yahweh.’
“Will you put them on trial? Will you, mortal one? Then show them the disgusting things their ancestors did.
Tell them that the Lord Yahweh says: ‘When I chose Israel, I made a solemn promise to Jacob’s family. I raised My hand and revealed Myself to them in Egypt. I said, “I am Yahweh your God.”
On that same day I promised to bring them out of Egypt. I would take them to a land I had searched out for them. It was rich with milk and honey, the finest of all lands.
I told them, “Each of you, get rid of the ugly idols you stare at. Do not make yourselves unclean with Egypt’s gods. I am Yahweh your God.”
“‘They rebelled, and they would not hear Me out. No one threw away his ugly idols. They did not leave Egypt’s gods behind. So I decided to let My anger pour out on them right there in Egypt.
Still, I held back, for My name’s sake. The nations around them had watched Me bring Israel out of that country, and I did not want My name treated as common in front of them.
I marched them away from Egypt and took them to the wilderness.
There I gave them My laws and taught them My decisions. Anyone who follows them will truly live.
My Sabbath days were another gift. Each one was meant to be a sign linking Me and them, a reminder to them that I am Yahweh, the One who makes them holy.

“‘Yet in the desert Israel’s people turned against Me. They would not follow My laws. They refused My decisions, even though following them gives life. They also made My Sabbaths very common. So I thought about pouring out My anger and ending them in the desert.
Once more My name made Me hold back. I did not want it dishonored among the nations that saw Me bring them out.
But out in the desert I lifted My hand and swore an oath. They would not enter the country I had given them, that land of milk and honey, finest of all.
They had refused My decisions and ignored My laws. They had made My Sabbaths common. Their hearts followed after their idols.
Even so, I felt sorry for them. I did not destroy them or finish them off in the desert.
“‘I spoke to their children in the desert. I said, “Do not live by your parents’ rules. Do not keep their customs. Do not make yourselves unclean with their idols.
I am Yahweh your God. Live by My laws. Keep My decisions and do them.
Treat My Sabbaths as holy. These days will mark the bond between us, and you will know that I, Yahweh, am your God.”

“‘But the children turned on Me too. They did not live by My laws. They were careless with My decisions, though those decisions give life to anyone who obeys. They made My Sabbaths common. So I thought about pouring out My anger on them in the desert until it was spent.
Yet I pulled My hand back. I held off because of My name, so it would not be dishonored among the nations that had seen Me bring them out.
But I also raised My hand in the desert and made another promise. I would send them far away and scatter them through many lands.
They had not done what I decided was right. They had refused My laws and made My Sabbaths common. Their eyes were set on the idols their parents had made.
So I handed them rules that were not good and customs that could not bring life.
I let their own gifts make them unclean, when they burned every first son in the fire.{b} I did it to horrify them, so they would know that I am Yahweh.’
“So now, mortal one, speak to Israel’s people. Tell them the Lord Yahweh says: ‘Your ancestors insulted Me in one more way. They were unfaithful to Me.

I had sworn with My raised hand to give them a land, and I took them there. But whenever they spotted a tall hill or a leafy tree, they offered sacrifices there. They brought gifts there that made Me angry. They burned sweet-smelling offerings there and poured out drinks there.
I asked them, “What is this high place you keep going to?” People still call it Bamah{c} today.’
“Tell Israel’s people that the Lord Yahweh says: ‘Will you make yourselves unclean the way your ancestors did? Will you chase after their ugly idols?

You bring gifts and burn your own sons in the fire. You are still making yourselves unclean with idols today. Should I then answer your questions, people of Israel? I swear by My own life, says the Lord Yahweh, that I will not answer your questions.
You say, “Let us be like the other nations, like the families of other lands, who worship wood and stone.” That idea will never come true.
“‘I swear by My own life, says the Lord Yahweh, that I will be your King. I will rule you with a strong hand, a stretched-out arm, and poured-out anger.
My strong hand, stretched-out arm, and poured-out anger will pull you out from among the peoples. I will collect you from every country where you were scattered.
I will take you to the desert of the nations. Face to face with you there, I will pass judgment.
In the desert near Egypt I judged your ancestors. In the same way I will judge you, says the Lord Yahweh.
I will have you walk under My shepherd’s rod, one by one. Then I will hold you to the terms of My agreement.{d}
I will remove the rebels who fight against Me. I will bring them out of the countries where they live as outsiders, but they will never enter Israel’s land. Then you will know that I am Yahweh.

“‘As for you, people of Israel, here is what the Lord Yahweh says. Go ahead, each of you, and serve your idols! But afterward, you will surely obey Me. You will stop dishonoring My holy name with your gifts and your idols.

The Lord Yahweh says that on My holy mountain, Israel’s high mountain, all of Israel will serve Me in their own land. I will be pleased with them there. I will ask for your offerings, the best of your gifts and everything you set apart for Me.

On the day I bring you out from the peoples and collect you from the places you were scattered, I will be pleased with you like the scent of sweet incense. The nations will watch Me show My holiness among you.
When I bring you into Israel’s land, the land I promised with a raised hand to give your ancestors, you will know that I am Yahweh.
There you will remember the way you lived and all you did that made you unclean. You will hate yourselves for all the evil you did.
People of Israel, I will treat you well for My name’s sake, not because of your evil ways or your rotten deeds. Then you will know that I am Yahweh, says the Lord Yahweh.’”
A message from Yahweh came to me again:{e}
“Mortal one, turn and face south. Preach against the south, and announce disaster for the forest of the Negev.{f}

Tell the southern forest, ‘Listen to Yahweh’s message. The Lord Yahweh says: Look, I will set you on fire. It will eat up every tree, green or dry. Nothing will stop the blazing flame. From the Negev to the far north, it will scorch every face.
Everyone will see that I, Yahweh, started this fire. No one can put it out.’”
Then I said, “Oh, Lord Yahweh! People say about me, ‘He only tells riddles.’”

notes.text: In Hebrew the date is “in the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month,” counting from the spring new year. The month was later called Av. The year was 591 BC. The Greek has only “on the fifteenth of the month.”
Or “when they gave up every first son.” Compare 16:21.
Bamah means “high place.” Ezekiel is playing with sounds in the question “What (mah) is the high place to which you go (ba’im)?”
The Greek has “and I will bring you in by number.” The meaning of the Hebrew word for “terms” is uncertain.
In Hebrew, 20:45–49 is numbered 21:1–5, and 21:1–32 is numbered 21:6–37.
The Negev is the dry region south of Judah. Here “south” also stands for Judah and Jerusalem (see 21:2).

subheads.1: Israel’s Long History of Turning Away
subheads.45: A Fire in the Southern Forest

verses.text: Yahweh’s message came to me again:
“Mortal one, turn toward Jerusalem and speak against its holy places. Announce trouble for the land of Israel.
Tell it that Yahweh says: ‘Look out, I have come for you. My sword leaves its case, and in you it will strike down good people and bad people alike.
Since I will cut down the good and the bad alike, My sword will leave its case and go against every living person, from the south all the way to the north.
Then everyone will know that I, Yahweh, pulled out My sword. It will not go back into its case.’
“And you, mortal one, groan! Let them watch you groan with a broken heart{a} and deep sorrow.

Some will ask, ‘Why do you groan?’ Answer, ‘News is on its way. Hearts will melt in fear, and hands will hang weak. Every spirit will faint, and every knee will turn to water. It is coming! It will surely happen, says the Lord Yahweh.’”
Yahweh spoke to me:

“Mortal one, prophesy. Say, ‘The Lord says: A sword! A sword!
It has been sharpened,
and it has been polished too.

The sword was given out to be polished
and held in the hand.
It is sharp and shiny,
ready for the killer to take up.’
Cry out and wail, mortal one. This sword is coming for My people and for all of Israel’s leaders. They will fall to it along with My people. So strike your leg in sorrow.{c}
A test has begun. What if the rod that looks down on others is gone for good? says the Lord Yahweh.{d}

“Now you, mortal one, clap your hands as you prophesy.
Twice the sword will fall, and even three times.
It is the sword that kills,
the sword of the great slaughter,
circling around them.

Their hearts will melt,
and many will trip and fall.
At every one of their gates I have set the sword that kills.{e}
See how it is made to gleam like lightning!
A hand is gripping it, ready to kill.

Slash to the right!
Then turn and slash to the left,
wherever your blade is pointed.

I will clap My hands too,
and My anger will be satisfied.
I, Yahweh, have spoken.”
Yahweh’s message came to me again:
“Mortal one, draw two roads on the ground for the Babylonian king’s sword to travel. Both roads begin in the same country. Set up a signpost where the road leads toward a city.
Draw one road for the sword to reach Rabbah, the Ammonite city. Draw another that leads to Judah and to Jerusalem, the city with strong walls.
The king of Babylon has halted where the road divides into two. He wants a sign. He shakes his arrows, asks his household gods,{f} and studies a sheep’s liver.

In his right hand, the marker says “Jerusalem.” So he will set up battering rams, order the killing, and shout the battle cry. He will set rams against the gates, pile up a dirt ramp, and build siege towers.
The people of Jerusalem have sworn serious oaths.{g} To them, this sign will seem false. Yet the king will bring their guilt back to mind, and that is how they will be caught.
“So the Lord Yahweh says: You have made your guilt clear. Your open rebellion and all your actions have shown your sins. Because you have been exposed, you will be grabbed by force.
And you, evil and unclean prince of Israel, your day has come. This is the time when your guilt ends in punishment.
The Lord Yahweh says: Take off the turban. Remove the crown. Things will not stay as they are. The low will be lifted up, and the high will be brought down.
I will make it a ruin, a ruin, a ruin! Even that will wait until the one comes who has the right to judge. Then I will give it to him.{h}

“And you, mortal one, prophesy. Say, ‘The Lord Yahweh says this about the Ammonites and their mocking:
A sword! A sword is drawn to kill.
It is polished to eat up everything,
to flash like lightning.

Your visions are empty,
and your signs are lies.
They will lay you on the necks of the wicked who are dead,
whose day has come,
the time when guilt ends in punishment.

Put the sword back in its case!
I will judge you at the spot where you were formed,
in the country you came from.

I will pour My fury over you.
I will blow on you with the fire of My anger.
I will give you to cruel men
who are experts at destroying.

You will be wood for the fire.
Your blood will soak the land.
No one will remember you,
for I, Yahweh, have spoken.’”

notes.text: Hebrew: “with breaking of the hips.”
The Hebrew of this line is very hard to understand, and any translation is a guess.
This was a sign of sorrow or alarm (see Jeremiah 31:19).
The Hebrew of verse 13 is very hard to understand.
The meaning of the Hebrew word translated “killing” here is uncertain.
The Hebrew word is teraphim, small statues used to seek messages (see Genesis 31:19).
The meaning of this Hebrew phrase is uncertain. It may mean the oaths of loyalty sworn to the king of Babylon.
Or “until the one comes whose right it is.” The wording is like Genesis 49:10.

subheads.18: Babylon’s King at the Fork in the Road

verses.text: Yahweh spoke to me, saying:
“Mortal one, are you ready to judge? Will you judge this city full of murder? Then make her face every disgusting thing she has done.
Tell her the Lord Yahweh says: ‘City, you spill blood inside your walls, and so your time of doom is coming. You also make idols that leave you unclean.

Blood you have spilled makes you guilty, and idols you have made make you unclean. You have brought your day close, and your years have run out. So I have made you a shame among the nations and a joke to every land.
Near or far, people will laugh at you, city with a stained name and a heart of chaos.
“‘See how Israel’s princes in you, each one using his power, work hard to shed blood.
Inside you, parents are hated. Inside you, outsiders are crushed. Inside you, orphans and widows are cheated.
You have looked down on My holy things and made My Sabbaths common.
In you are men who spread lies to get people killed. In you are men who eat at the shrines on the hills. In you people do shameful sexual acts.
