In you, men have sex with their fathers’ wives.{a} In you, men attack women during their time of monthly uncleanness.
One man does a disgusting thing with his neighbor’s wife. Another shames his own daughter-in-law. Another attacks his sister, the daughter of his own father.
In you, people take bribes to kill. You lend money for extra payment and gain wealth by cheating your neighbors. You have forgotten Me completely. This is the Lord Yahweh’s word.
“‘So now I strike My hands together at the money you stole and the blood spilled in you.
Can you stay brave? Can your hands stay strong when the day comes for Me to deal with you? I, Yahweh, have given My word, and I will carry it out.
I will scatter you among the nations and send you across many lands. I will end the filth that is in you.
You will be shamed{b} because of what you did, while the nations watch. After that, you will know who I am: Yahweh.’”
A message from Yahweh came to me:
“Mortal one, to Me the people of Israel are waste left over from melting. Inside the furnace, they are all copper, tin, iron, and lead. They are the useless scraps left from silver.
So the Lord Yahweh says: Every one of you has become scrap, and so I will pull you together into Jerusalem.
People put silver, copper, iron, lead, and tin into a furnace, blow on the fire, and melt them. In the same way I will pile you in the city in My anger and fury, and I will melt you there.
I will round you up, breathe My burning rage over you, and let the city melt you down.
Silver melts in a furnace, and so you will melt inside Jerusalem. Then you will know that I, Yahweh, have poured My fury out on you.”
Yahweh’s message came to me:
“Mortal one, tell her, ‘You are a land that was never cleaned. No rain fell on you on the day of My anger.’
Her prophets{c} have made a plot inside her. They are like a lion that roars and tears its catch apart. They eat up lives, take treasure and valuable things, and leave many women widows.

Her priests twist My teaching and treat My holy things as common. They do not tell the holy from the ordinary. They never teach the difference between clean and unclean. They look away from My Sabbaths, and so I am dishonored among them.
Her officials are like wolves that tear apart their catch. They kill and destroy lives to make dishonest money.
Her prophets cover up all these sins like paint over a crack. They see false visions and tell lies. They say, ‘The Lord Yahweh says this,’ when Yahweh has not spoken.
The people of the land cheat and steal. They mistreat the poor and needy. They are unfair to outsiders and give them no justice.
I searched among them for one man to rebuild the wall and stand in the broken place in front of Me, to protect the land from My destroying it. But I found no one.
So I have poured My anger out on them. I have burned them up with the fire of My rage. I have made them pay for how they lived, says the Lord Yahweh.”

notes.text: Hebrew: “A father’s nakedness is uncovered.” This means sexual relations with a father’s wife (see Leviticus 18:8).
So the main Hebrew text. The Greek reads differently: “I will give inheritances in you.”
The Greek has “her princes.” Many scholars prefer this because prophets are talked about again in verse 28.

verses.text: Yahweh spoke to me again:
“Mortal one, picture two women who were born to the same mother.
While still young in Egypt, they gave themselves to wrong lovers. In that land they let men treat them shamefully.
Two sisters, one older and one younger: Oholah{a} was the elder, and Oholibah{b} the younger. Both belonged to Me, and both bore children. As a picture, Oholah is Samaria, and Oholibah is Jerusalem.
“Oholah was Mine, yet she turned away and chased other lovers. She longed for the Assyrians, her neighbors,{c}
who wore blue uniforms. They were governors and officers, handsome young men, all riding horses.
She gave herself to the best men of Assyria, and she made herself unclean with the idols of each man she wanted.
She never gave up the habits she learned in Egypt, where men had used her since her youth and poured out their desire on her.
So I handed her over to the lovers she wanted so much, the Assyrians.
Those lovers stripped her bare. Her children were seized, and she herself died by the sword. Other women whispered her name as a warning, because justice had come to her.
“Her sister Oholibah watched all this. Even so, her desire was worse than Oholah’s, and her unfaithfulness went further.
She also wanted the Assyrians: governors and officers in splendid clothes, handsome young men riding horses.
I saw that she was unclean too. Both sisters went down the same path.
But Oholibah went even further. She saw pictures of Chaldean men painted in red on a wall.
They wore belts at their waists and long, flowing headcloths. Each looked like a Babylonian chief from the land of Chaldea.
When she saw them, she wanted them at once. So she sent messengers to Chaldea.
Babylon’s men came to her bed of love and made her unclean. Then, once they were done, she could not stand the sight of them.
Because she showed off her sin so openly, I turned from her in disgust, just as I had turned from her sister.
Still, she sinned more and more, remembering her youth in Egypt.
There she had wanted men who were crude and rough like animals.
So you missed the shameful days of your youth in Egypt, Oholibah.
“Therefore, Oholibah, the Lord Yahweh says: Listen! I will stir up the lovers you turned from in disgust. I will bring them against you from every side.

Babylonians and Chaldeans will come, with the people of Pekod, Shoa, and Koa.{d} All Assyria will join them: handsome young men, governors and chiefs, officers and famous leaders, every one on horseback.

Chariots, wagons, and a huge crowd of nations will march on you from the north.{e} They will take positions all around you with large shields, small shields, and helmets. I will hand the judging over to them, and they will punish you by their own laws.

My fierce jealousy will fall on you, and they will act in rage. Your nose and ears will be cut off. Whoever remains will die by the sword. Your sons and daughters will be dragged away, and fire will eat up whatever is left.
They will take off your clothes and take away your fine jewelry.
So I will end the shameful life you brought out of Egypt. You will not look up to those lovers or think about Egypt again.
“The Lord Yahweh says: I am putting you into the hands of the people you hate, the ones you turned from in disgust.
They will hate you and take all you worked for. They will leave you bare and ashamed, and your shameful life will be out in the open.
This will happen because you chased after the nations and made yourself unclean with their idols.
Your sister walked a road, and you walked it too. So I give her cup to you.

“The Lord Yahweh says:
You will drink the cup your sister drank,
a cup deep and wide.
People will mock you and laugh,
for the cup holds so much.

You will be full of drunkenness and sorrow.
It is a cup of horror and ruin,
the cup of your sister Samaria.

You will drink it to the last drop
and even chew on the broken pieces,
and you will hurt yourself in your grief.
I have spoken, says the Lord Yahweh.
“So the Lord Yahweh says: You put Me out of your mind and walked away from Me. Now you must bear what your shameful life has earned.”
Then Yahweh asked me, “Mortal one, are you ready to judge Oholah and Oholibah? Then make them face their disgusting deeds.
They have been unfaithful, and their hands are stained with blood. They were unfaithful with idols. They even burned the children they bore to Me, giving them to those idols as food.
They did something more against Me. On that same day they made My holy place unclean and made My Sabbaths common.
On the very day they killed their children for their idols, they walked into My holy place and made it unclean. They did this inside My own house.
“They even sent far away for men. A messenger went out, and the men arrived. For their visit you washed, put paint around your eyes, and dressed up in jewels.
There was a grand couch, and in front of it a table. On the table you laid out incense and oil that belonged to Me.
A careless, noisy crowd surrounded her, with rough men from the desert{f} mixed in. Bracelets were slipped onto the women’s wrists, and beautiful crowns were set on their heads.
Then I said about the woman worn out by unfaithfulness, ‘Now they will use her like this, even her!’
And the men came to her as men go to a prostitute. That is how they came to Oholah and Oholibah, those shameless women.
But fair and good men will judge them as women who were unfaithful and who spilled blood, because that is what they are.
“The Lord Yahweh says: Call a crowd against them. Give them over to terror and robbing.
A mob will throw stones at them and cut them down with swords. Their children will be killed, and their houses set on fire.
So I will stop shameful living in the land, and every woman will learn not to act as you did.
You will be paid back for your shameful acts and carry the guilt of your sins with idols. Then you will know that I am the Lord Yahweh.”

notes.text: Oholah means “her tent.” It may point to the shrines Samaria built for herself.
Oholibah means “my tent is in her.” It points to Yahweh’s temple in Jerusalem.
Or “who were near.” The Hebrew word can mean “near.”
Pekod, Shoa, and Koa were peoples east of the Tigris River. The names may also be word plays in Hebrew.
The Hebrew word here is uncertain. Some old copies read “from the north.”
Or “Sabeans,” following the written Hebrew; the meaning is uncertain.

verses.text: On the tenth day of the tenth month (in December–January) of the ninth year,{a} Yahweh spoke to me:
“Mortal one, write down today’s date. On this very day, the king of Babylon has begun his siege of Jerusalem.

Tell this story to the rebellious people. Say to them, ‘The Lord Yahweh says:
Put the cooking pot on the fire.
Pour water in it.

Drop in the pieces of meat,
all the good cuts, thigh and shoulder.
Fill it up with the best bones.

Choose the best sheep from the flock.
Stack the logs{b} beneath the pot.
Let it bubble hard,
and cook the bones inside.

“‘The Lord Yahweh says:
How terrible for the city full of blood!
She is a pot with crust{c} stuck inside,
a crust that will not come off.
Pull the meat out one piece at a time.
No one gets picked or spared.{d}

Her murder is not hidden.
She left the blood on a bare rock,
not on the ground
where dust could cover it.

I left her blood on the bare rock
so it would not be hidden.
It cries out for anger and payback.

“‘The Lord Yahweh says:
How terrible for the city full of blood!
I Myself will build her fire high.

Pile on the wood and light the flame.
Boil the meat down,
stir in the spices,{e}
and let the bones scorch.

Then set the empty pot on the hot coals
until the copper glows red.
The filth inside will melt,
and the crust will burn away.
Your filth is your shameful living. I tried to wash you clean, but you would not be clean. You will stay dirty until My anger against you has been spent.

I am Yahweh, and I have said it. The time has come, and I will do it. I will not hold back, feel sorry, or change My mind. You will be judged by the way you lived and what you did, says the Lord Yahweh.’”
Yahweh spoke to me again:
“Mortal one, with one sudden blow I am taking away the one you love most. Even so, do not mourn, cry, or let tears fall.
Groan quietly, and do not hold a funeral. Keep your headcloth on and your sandals on your feet. Do not cover your mouth, and do not eat the food friends bring to people in grief.”{g}
That morning I preached to the people. By nightfall my wife was dead. At dawn the next day I acted out my orders.
Then the people asked, “What do these actions mean? Tell us how they touch us.”
I answered, “Yahweh gave me a message.

He said, ‘Say to Israel’s people, “The Lord Yahweh says: I will soon make My own temple unclean. You are proud of its strength. Your eyes love it, and your hearts long for it. The children you had to leave in the city will be killed by swords.
You will copy me. Your mouths will stay uncovered, and you will refuse the food friends bring in times of grief.
Your headcloths will stay on, and your sandals will stay on your feet. You will not mourn or cry. Instead you will rot away in your guilt, and you will groan to each other.
Ezekiel is a sign for you. Whatever he did, you will do. When that day comes, you will know that I am the Lord Yahweh.”’
“As for you, mortal one, that day is coming. I will take away their safe fortress, the glad pride they love, and the dear sons and daughters their hearts long for.
Someone who escaped will walk up to you and tell you the news.
When he arrives, your mouth will open. You will speak freely and no longer stay silent. So you will be a sign to them, and they will know that I am Yahweh.”

notes.text: Hebrew: “in the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth of the month.” The year counts from spring, and this date is about January 588 BC.
Or “bones”; compare verse 10.
Or “rust” or “scum.” The meaning of the Hebrew word is uncertain; it also appears in verses 11 and 12.
Hebrew: “no lot has fallen on it.” That is, no piece is set aside to be saved.
The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain. Some read “pour out the broth.”
The Hebrew of this line is uncertain.
Hebrew: “the bread of men.” Many scholars read “the bread of mourners.”

verses.text: Yahweh spoke to me again.
“Mortal one, look toward the land of Ammon.{a} Speak a message against its people.
Tell them, ‘Hear what the Lord Yahweh says. You cheered when My holy place was made unclean. You cheered when Israel’s land was left empty. You cheered when Judah’s people were dragged away.
So I am handing you over to the tribes of the eastern desert. They will camp in your land and build their homes there. They will eat your fruit and drink your milk.
Your city Rabbah will become a pasture for camels, and your towns will become pens for sheep. Then you will know that I am Yahweh.
“Here is what the Lord Yahweh says: With clapping hands and stomping feet, you laughed with deep scorn over the land of Israel.
So I have raised My hand against you. I will give you away as loot to the nations. I will remove you from the earth and wipe out your kingdom. Then you will know that I am Yahweh.’
“The Lord Yahweh says: Moab and Seir{b} said, ‘Judah’s people are no different from any other nation.’
So I will open up Moab’s side and leave its best towns unguarded. These are its border towns, the pride of its land: Beth-jeshimoth, Baal-meon, and Kiriathaim.{c}
I will hand Moab to the tribes of the eastern desert, just as I do with Ammon. No one will remember Ammon among the nations any longer.
Moab will feel My punishment. Only then will they know that I am Yahweh.
“The Lord Yahweh says: Edom got even with the people of Judah. Edom took cruel revenge and became very guilty.

So the Lord Yahweh says: I will raise My hand against Edom. I will remove its people and animals. The land will become a wasteland, and they will die in battle, from the town of Teman all the way to Dedan.{d}
My own people Israel will carry out My revenge on Edom. They will treat Edom as My anger and rage demand. Then Edom will learn what My revenge is like, says the Lord Yahweh.
“The Lord Yahweh says: The Philistines took their revenge. They held an old hatred, and they tried to destroy Judah with spite in their hearts.
So the Lord Yahweh says: My hand will rise against the Philistines. The Cherethites{e} will be wiped out by Me, and I will destroy everyone left along the coast.
I will pay them back hard, with angry punishment. When I take My revenge, they will know that I am Yahweh.”

notes.text: Ammon lay east of the Jordan River. Its capital was Rabbah, which is the modern city of Amman in Jordan.
Seir is the hill country of Edom. The Septuagint does not have “and Seir.”
Beth-jeshimoth may mean “house of the deserts.” Baal-meon may mean “owner of the home.” Kiriathaim means “double city.”
Teman was a region in the north of Edom. Dedan was an oasis town in Arabia to the south.
The Cherethites were a people who lived with the Philistines. They may have come from Crete.

verses.text: In the eleventh year, on the first day of the month,{a} Yahweh spoke to me:
“Mortal one, Tyre{b} has gloated over Jerusalem. She said, ‘Good! The gate to the nations is smashed, and it has swung open to me. Now that Jerusalem is a ruin, I will grow rich.’
So the Lord Yahweh says: Tyre, I am against you. I will bring many nations against you, as the sea throws wave after wave at the shore.
They will tear down Tyre’s walls and break her towers apart. I will scrape her dirt away and leave her a bare rock.
Fishermen will spread their nets on her rock in the middle of the sea. This is My promise, says the Lord Yahweh. She will become loot for the nations.
Her villages{c} on the mainland will fall to the sword, and by this they will learn that I am Yahweh.
“The Lord Yahweh says: I am bringing King Nebuchadrezzar{d} of Babylon against Tyre from the north. He is the king over kings. He comes with horses, chariots, riders, and a huge army.
He will kill your mainland villages with the sword. He will build towers against you, pile up a dirt ramp, and lift up a roof of shields.
He will pound your walls with rams, and he will smash your towers with iron tools.
So many horses will come that clouds of dust will bury you. At the roar of riders, wheels, and chariots your walls will shudder, as he marches in through your gates like an army into a broken city.
Hooves will beat down every street you have. Swords will kill your people, and your great pillars will fall to the ground.
Soldiers will steal your riches and carry off what you sell. Your walls will be torn down, and your fine houses wrecked. Your stones, wood, and dust will be thrown into the sea.
I will stop your noisy songs, and no one will hear your harps again.
Your rock will be bare, and fishermen will dry their nets on it. You will never be built again. I, Yahweh, have given My word, says the Lord Yahweh.
“The Lord Yahweh says to Tyre: The shores of the sea will shake when you fall. The wounded will groan, and the killing will go on inside you.

Then every prince along the sea will step down from his throne. They will lay aside their robes and take off their fancy clothes. Fear will be their only clothing. They will sit on the ground, shaking and stunned at what happened to you.

They will chant a funeral song for you: ‘How you have vanished from the seas,
city of fame!
You and your people ruled the waves
and filled everyone nearby with fear.

Now the islands shake with fear
on the day you fall.
Out in the sea, the islands
are stunned that you are gone.’
“The Lord Yahweh says: I will make you a ruin, like towns where no one lives. I will bring the deep water over you, and the great waves will cover you.

Then I will send you down to the pit,{e} to join the people of long ago. You will live in the world below, among old ruins, with those who went down before you. Never again will you have a home{f} in the land of the living.
Your end will fill people with horror. You will be gone. Search for you as they may, they will never find you, says the Lord Yahweh.”

notes.text: Hebrew: “in the eleventh year, on the first of the month.” The month is not named. The year is about 587 or 586 BC.
Tyre means “rock.” It was a rich Phoenician port, built mostly on an island just off the coast.
Hebrew: “daughters.” These were the small towns that depended on Tyre. The word is also used in verse 8.
Hebrew: Nebuchadrezzar. This spelling is closer to the Babylonian name, which may mean “Nabu, protect my son.”
The pit means the place of the dead.
The Septuagint says “give glory.” The Hebrew says “take your stand.”

subheads.19: Tyre Goes Down to the Pit

verses.text: Yahweh spoke to me:
“Mortal one, sing a funeral song for Tyre.

Tell Tyre, the city at the harbor of the sea, who trades with the peoples of many shores, that the Lord Yahweh says:
Tyre, you bragged,
‘My beauty is perfect.’

Your land lay out in the open sea.
Your builders made you lovely.

They shaped your boards
from fir trees of Senir.{a}
They picked a cedar of Lebanon
and made your mast from it.

They carved your oars
from oak trees of Bashan.
Your deck was ivory
set in cypress wood{b} from the shores of Kittim.{c}

Your sail was linen from Egypt,
with bright stitching,
and it flew like a flag.
Your awnings were blue and purple
from the shores of Elishah.{d}

Men from Sidon and Arvad{e} pulled your oars.
Your own wise men, Tyre, were your sailors.

Old and skilled men from Gebal{f}
patched the cracks in your sides.
Every ship on the sea, with its crew,
docked at your port to trade.
“‘Soldiers from Persia, Lud, and Put{g} filled your army. Their shields and helmets hung inside your city, and they gave you your glory.
Men of Arvad, along with your own army, guarded your walls on every side. Men of Gammad{h} stood in your towers. Shields hung around your walls, and they made your beauty complete.
“‘Tarshish{i} did business with you because you had so much of everything. Silver, iron, tin, and lead were their payment for your goods.
Javan,{j} Tubal, and Meshech{k} bought from you. They paid with slaves and with bronze pots and pans.
Beth-togarmah{l} paid you with work horses, war horses, and mules.
The people of Dedan{m} traded with you, and many shores were your customers. Tusks of ivory and logs of ebony were their payment.
Aram{n} did business with you because you made so many goods. They paid with green gems, purple cloth, stitched cloth, fine linen, coral, and red stones.
Judah and Israel traded with you too. They paid with wheat from Minnith, sweets and grain,{o} honey, olive oil, and healing balm.
Damascus bought from you because you made so many things and had so much wealth. They paid with wine from Helbon and wool from Zahar.{p}
From Uzal{q} came wine, iron bars, cassia, and sweet cane, in trade for what you sold.
Dedan sold you blankets for riding.
Arabia and all the chiefs of Kedar{r} were your buyers. They paid with lambs, rams, and goats.
Sheba and Raamah{s} sent merchants to trade with you. They brought the best spices, every kind of gem, and gold for your goods.
Haran, Canneh, and Eden traded with you. So did Sheba’s merchants, Asshur, and Chilmad.{t}
In your market they sold you fine clothes, blue cloaks, stitched cloth, and colorful rugs tied with strong cords.

Ships of Tarshish carried your goods.
You were loaded down,
heavy in the middle of the sea.

“‘Your rowers took you
far out on the deep water.
There the east wind wrecked you
in the middle of the sea.

All your wealth, goods, and trade,
your sailors and steersmen,
your ship repairers and merchants,
and every soldier on board,
with the whole crowd inside you,
will sink to the bottom of the sea
on the day of your wreck.

When your steersmen cry out,
the shores{u} will shake.

Everyone who pulls an oar
will climb down from the ships.
The sailors and all the steersmen
will stand on the land.

They will cry out loud over you
and weep bitterly.
Dust will fly onto their heads,
and they will sit down in ashes.

They will cut off their hair for you
and wear rough sackcloth.
Their hearts will break as they weep,
in bitter sorrow.{v}

In their sorrow they will sing a funeral song for you:
“Who was ever like Tyre,
now silent{w} in the middle of the sea?”

When your goods came in from the sea,
you satisfied many nations.
Your huge wealth and trade
brought riches to kings across the world.

Now the sea has wrecked you.
You lie in deep water.
Your goods and your whole crew
have sunk with you.

Everyone who lives along the coasts
is stunned over you.
Their kings shudder in fear,
and their faces twist in horror.

The traders among the nations whistle in shock.
Your end has filled people with terror,
and you will be gone forever.’”

notes.text: Senir is another name for Mount Hermon.
The Hebrew word is uncertain. It may mean “pine” or “boxwood,” or it may be read as “daughter of the Assyrians.”
Kittim means Cyprus, named for the city of Kition. Later the name was used for western lands in general.
Elishah is probably Alashiya, an old name for Cyprus or part of it.
Arvad was a Phoenician city on an island north of Tyre.
Gebal is the city the Greeks called Byblos. It was a Phoenician port north of Sidon.
Lud is probably Lydia in Asia Minor. Put is probably Libya.
No one knows where Gammad was. The Septuagint says “guards.”
Tarshish was a far western port, probably in Spain. The Septuagint says “Carthaginians.”
Javan means Greece, or the Greek coast of Asia Minor.
Tubal and Meshech were peoples in central Asia Minor.
Beth-togarmah was a land in eastern Asia Minor, probably near Armenia.
This follows the main Hebrew text. The Septuagint says “Rhodians.”
Some ancient copies say “Edom.” In Hebrew the two names look almost the same.
The meaning of the Hebrew word for “sweets and grain” is uncertain. It may name a kind of millet.
Or “white wool.”
The Hebrew of this verse is uncertain. “From Uzal” may belong with the list of goods.
Kedar was a tribe in the Arabian desert.
Sheba and Raamah were peoples in southern Arabia.
Chilmad is not known. The other names are trade centers in Mesopotamia and Arabia.
Or “pasturelands.” The meaning is uncertain.
The Septuagint does not have verse 31.
The Hebrew word is uncertain. Some read “like a ruin.”

subheads.1: A Song of Sorrow for Tyre

verses.text: Yahweh spoke to me:

“Mortal one, give the ruler of Tyre this message from the Lord Yahweh:
Pride fills your heart.
You claim, ‘I am divine!
My seat is a throne for the gods,
far out in the sea.’
Yet you are a human being, no god at all,
though you imagine your mind equals the mind of God.

In your own eyes you are wiser than Daniel.{a}
You believe no mystery can be kept from you.

Your wisdom and your skill
brought you great wealth.
Gold and silver are heaped up
in your storerooms.

Your clever trading
has made your wealth grow,
and your riches
have made you proud.

“So the Lord Yahweh says:
You think your mind
is as wise as God’s.

Because of this, I am sending strangers against you,
the cruelest of all nations.
They will pull out their swords against your wise and lovely city
and ruin your glory.

When your killer faces you,
will you still say, ‘I am a god’?
In the hands of those who stab you,
you will see that you are a man and not a god.
Yahweh spoke to me:

Eden, the garden of God, was your home.
Jewels of every kind covered you:
red stone, yellow stone, and diamond,
sea-green stone, onyx, and jasper,
blue stone, turquoise, and emerald.{e}
Your settings were made of gold,
all prepared when you were made.

Your busy trading
filled you with cruelty,
and you sinned.
So I threw you off God’s mountain in shame.
I drove you out, guardian angel,
away from the stones of fire.

You grew proud because you were so handsome.
Your glory spoiled your good sense.
I threw you down to the ground.
I put you in front of kings,
and they stared at you.

You did so much wrong
and cheated so many people
that you made your holy places unclean.
So I made a fire come out of you,
and it burned you to nothing.
On the ground I left only ashes,
for everyone to see.

All the nations that knew you
are shocked at you.
Your end has filled people with terror,
and you are gone forever.”
Yahweh spoke to me:
“Mortal one, look toward Sidon.{g} Speak a message against her.
Say, ‘The Lord Yahweh says: Sidon, I am against you. My glory will be seen in your midst. People will know that I am Yahweh when I punish her and show My holiness through her.
I will send a sickness into her and blood into her streets. Dead people will lie inside her, struck down by swords on every side. By this they will learn that I am Yahweh.
“‘Israel’s people will no longer have neighbors who hate them and hurt them like sharp thorns and stinging weeds. Then they will know that I am the Lord Yahweh.

“‘This is the promise of the Lord Yahweh: Israel’s people are scattered among the nations. I will gather them up. I will show My holiness through them while the nations watch. At last they will settle on their own soil, the land I gave My servant Jacob.
They will live there in peace. They will build houses and plant vineyards. They will live safely when I punish all the neighbors who hated them. Then they will know that I am Yahweh their God.’”

notes.text: The Hebrew spelling is Danel. See the note at 14:14.
The pit means the place of the dead.
Hebrew: “the death of the uncircumcised.” This meant a shameful death, without an honored burial.
The Hebrew phrase is unclear. It may mean “the one who sets the pattern of a perfect shape.”
The Hebrew names nine stones. Scholars are not sure what some of them are.
Or “You were with a guardian angel.” The Hebrew has an unusual form here. The Septuagint says “with the cherub.” A cherub is a winged guardian being.
Sidon was about 25 miles (40 kilometers) north of Tyre. It was the other great Phoenician city.

subheads.11: A Song of Sorrow for the King
subheads.20: Sidon, and a Promise for Israel

verses.text: On the twelfth day of the tenth month (in December–January) of the tenth year,{a} Yahweh spoke to me:
“Mortal one, turn toward Pharaoh, the king of Egypt. Preach against him, and against every part of Egypt.

Give this message: The Lord Yahweh says:
I am against you,
Pharaoh, king of Egypt,
great river monster,{b}
lying in the streams of your Nile.
You boast, ‘This river is mine.
I made it for my own use.’

I will put hooks in your jaws,
and the fish of your streams will cling to your scales.
Then I will pull you out of your streams,
with every fish still stuck to you.

I will toss you into the desert,
you and every fish from your rivers.
You will land in an open field,
and no one will lift you or bury you.
I have handed you over to wild animals and birds
for food.

Then all who live in Egypt will learn
that I am Yahweh.
For Israel’s people leaned on Egypt
as on a weak reed stick.

When Israel grabbed you with the hand,{c} you split
and cut their shoulders open.
When they leaned on you, you broke
and left their backs shaking.{d}
“The Lord Yahweh says: I am bringing a sword against you, and it will cut down your people and your animals.
Egypt will become a dry and empty ruin, and they will come to know that I am Yahweh. Pharaoh said, ‘The Nile is mine. I made it.’
Therefore I stand against you and your streams. I will leave Egypt a ruin and a wasteland, all the way from Migdol at one end to Syene{e} at the other, even to the border of Cush.{f}
No human foot or animal foot will cross the land. For forty years, nobody will make a home there.

I will make Egypt the emptiest land of all. Its cities will lie in ruins, emptier than any other city, for forty years. I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and spread them across the lands.
“Still, the Lord Yahweh says: After forty years pass, I will pick up the Egyptians from among the peoples where they were scattered.
They will return from captivity to Pathros,{g} the land of their fathers. There they will form a small, weak kingdom.
It will be the weakest of all kingdoms. It will never again rise over the other nations. I will make Egypt so small that it can never rule them.
Israel’s people will never again trust in Egypt. Instead, Egypt will remind them of their sin in asking it for help. And they will know that I am the Lord Yahweh.”
In the twenty-seventh year, on the first day of the first month (in March–April),{h} Yahweh spoke to me:

“Mortal one, King Nebuchadrezzar of Babylon made his army work very hard against Tyre. Every soldier’s head was rubbed bare by helmets, and every shoulder was rubbed raw by loads. Yet neither the king nor his army earned any pay from Tyre for all that work.
So the Lord Yahweh says: Egypt’s land is My gift to King Nebuchadrezzar of Babylon. He will haul off its wealth.{i} He will grab its goods and loot its treasures. This will be the pay for his army.
I am giving him Egypt as his reward for his work, because his army was really working for Me, says the Lord Yahweh.
“Someday I will make a horn{j} grow for Israel’s people. I will also let you speak freely among them, and they will learn that I am Yahweh.”

notes.text: Hebrew: “in the tenth year, in the tenth month, on the twelfth of the month.” The year counts from spring, so this date is about January 587 BC.
Hebrew: tannim. This is a kind of sea monster or dragon. Here it stands for the Nile crocodile.
This follows the Hebrew margin and the Septuagint. The Hebrew text says “by your palm.”
The Hebrew is probably “made their hips shake.” The Septuagint says “crushed all their backs.” Some Hebrew copies say “made them stand.”
Migdol was in the northeast of Egypt, and Syene (modern Aswan) was in the far south. The phrase means “from one end of Egypt to the other.”
Cush was the upper Nile region, in modern Sudan.
Pathros means Upper Egypt, the south.
Hebrew: “in the twenty-seventh year, in the first month, on the first of the month.” The year counts from spring, so this date is about April 571 BC.
Or “its crowd.”
A horn stands for strength.

subheads.8: Egypt Will Be Empty for Forty Years
subheads.17: Egypt as Pay for Babylon’s Army

verses.text: Yahweh spoke to me:

“Mortal one, give this message: The Lord Yahweh says:
Cry out, ‘Oh, what a terrible day!’

The day is close.
Yahweh’s day is close.
It is a dark and cloudy day,
a time of ruin for the nations.

A sword will strike Egypt,
and Cush will writhe in pain.
Egypt’s dead will lie on the ground,
her riches will be hauled off,
and her foundations will be torn up.

Cush, Put, Lud, the whole mixed crowd,{a} Cub,{b} and the people of the allied land{c}
will fall by the sword together with Egypt.

“Yahweh says:
Those who hold Egypt up will fall,
and her proud strength will sink.
From Migdol to Syene
the sword will cut her people down,
says the Lord Yahweh.

Egypt will be a ruin
among ruined lands,
and her cities will stand empty
among wrecked cities.

When I set Egypt on fire
and break all her helpers,
they will know that I am Yahweh.
“On that day I will send out messengers by ship to scare the careless people of Cush. They will tremble on Egypt’s day of doom. It is coming!

“The Lord Yahweh says:
Egypt’s great crowd will come to an end
through King Nebuchadrezzar of Babylon.

The king and his army,
the cruelest of nations,
are on their way to ruin the land.
Their swords will come out against Egypt,
and dead bodies will cover the ground.

I will dry up the Nile’s streams,
and I will sell the land to wicked men.
Through strangers I will ruin
the land and all that is in it.
I, Yahweh, have said it.

“The Lord Yahweh says:
The idols will be wiped out,
and Memphis’s worthless gods{d} will be gone.
Egypt will never again have a prince of its own,
and I will fill the land with fear.

I will set fire to Egypt.
Pelusium will twist in pain.
Thebes will be broken open,
and Memphis will face enemies in daylight.{h}

In Tehaphnehes{l} the day will turn dark{m}
when I break Egypt’s yokes there.
Her proud strength will end in that city.
She will be covered with clouds,
and her daughters will be taken away.

In this way I will punish Egypt,
and they will know that I am Yahweh.”
On the seventh day of the first month (in March–April) of the eleventh year,{n} Yahweh spoke to me:
“Mortal one, Pharaoh’s arm, the arm of Egypt’s king, is broken by Me. No one has bandaged it so that it can heal. No one has tied on a splint so that it can grip a sword again.
Here is what the Lord Yahweh says: Pharaoh, king of Egypt, is My enemy. His strong arm and his broken arm will both be snapped. His sword will drop out of his hand.
I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and spread them across the lands.
Babylon’s king will get strong arms from Me, and I will place My sword in his grip. But Pharaoh’s arms will be shattered, and he will groan in front of that king like a man dying of wounds.
I will hold up the arms of Babylon’s king, but Pharaoh’s arms will fall limp. When I put My sword in the hand of Babylon’s king, and he swings it over Egypt, they will know that I am Yahweh.
I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and spread them across the lands. Then they will come to know that I am Yahweh.”

notes.text: Or “all the Arabs.” The Hebrew letters can be read either way. The Septuagint list is different.
Cub is not known elsewhere. Many scholars read “Lub,” which means Libya.
Hebrew: “the sons of the land of the covenant.” The Septuagint says “the sons of My covenant.”
Hebrew: Noph. It was the old capital of Lower Egypt, near modern Cairo. The name is also used in verse 16.
Zoan, which the Greeks called Tanis, was in the northeast Nile delta.
Hebrew: No. It was the great city of Upper Egypt, near modern Luxor. The name is also used in verses 15 and 16.
Hebrew: Sin. The name is also used in verse 16. Pelusium was a border fortress in the northeast delta.
The Hebrew is uncertain. The Septuagint says “and waters will be poured out.”
Hebrew: Aven, which means “wickedness.” It is a play on On, the city the Greeks called Heliopolis, “city of the sun.”
Pi-beseth, which the Greeks called Bubastis, was in the eastern delta.
Hebrew: “they.” The word is feminine and probably means the towns. The Septuagint says “the women.”
Tehaphnehes, also spelled Tahpanhes, was the fortress of Daphnae in the northeast delta.
This follows the Septuagint and some other ancient copies. The main Hebrew text says “will hold back.”
Hebrew: “in the eleventh year, in the first month, on the seventh of the month.” The year counts from spring, so this date is about April 587 BC.

subheads.1: The Day of Yahweh Against Egypt

verses.text: On the first day of the third month (in May–June) of the eleventh year,{a} Yahweh spoke to me:

“Mortal one, tell Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, and all his people:
Who is as great as you?

Think about Assyria,{b} a cedar of Lebanon.
It had lovely branches and shady leaves like a forest.
It stood so tall
that its top reached the clouds.{c}

Water made it grow.
Deep springs lifted it high.
Streams flowed
all around where it stood,
and ditches carried water
to every tree in the field.

So it rose higher
than any other tree in the field.
Its limbs multiplied,
and its branches stretched out far
because it had so much water.

Every bird of the sky
built a nest in its limbs.
Under its branches,
wild animals gave birth to their young.
Great nations of every kind
sat in its cool shade.

It was beautiful and grand,
with long, spreading limbs,
because its roots reached down
to plenty of water.

Not even the cedars in God’s garden
could match it.
No fir tree had branches like these,
and no plane tree{d} had limbs
as grand as its limbs.
In God’s garden,
nothing was as lovely.

I gave it its beauty
and its thick branches.
In Eden, the garden of God,
every tree was jealous of it.
“So the Lord Yahweh says: That tree{e} grew very tall and pushed its top into the clouds. Its heart grew proud because of its height.
So I gave it to the strongest ruler among the nations. He treated it just as its evil deserved. I threw it out.

Strangers, the cruelest of nations, chopped it down and left it there. Its limbs dropped onto the mountains and into every valley. Broken branches lay in every gully of the land. All the peoples of the earth walked out of its shade and left it.

Now all the birds of the sky nest on its fallen trunk,
and all the wild animals
rest among its branches.

This will keep any tree by the water from growing so proud. None will push its top into the clouds, and none that drinks plenty of water{f} will stand that tall. Every one of them is promised to death, to the world below. They will join other mortals and the people who sink into the pit.

“The Lord Yahweh says: The day that tree dropped into Sheol,{g} the deep waters cried for it, because I closed them over it.{h} I held back its rivers, and the great waters stopped. I wrapped Lebanon in sadness for it, and every tree of the field drooped.

The nations shook at the sound of its crash, when I sent it down to Sheol to join the people of the pit. Then all the trees of Eden, the best and finest of Lebanon, every tree that drinks from the water, felt comforted in the world below.
Those trees went down to Sheol too, to join people killed by the sword. These were its strong arm,{i} the ones who had lived in its shade among the nations.

“Which tree in Eden is as glorious and great as you? Yet you will be thrown down to the world below beside those trees. You will lie among people who were never circumcised,{j} with those killed by the sword. That is Pharaoh and all his people, says the Lord Yahweh.”

notes.text: Hebrew: “in the eleventh year, in the third month, on the first of the month.” The year counts from spring, so this date is about June 587 BC.
Some scholars read one Hebrew letter differently and find “a cypress tree” here instead of “Assyria.”
This follows the Septuagint. The Hebrew word may mean “thick leaves.” It is also used in verses 10 and 14.
No one is sure which trees these are.
Hebrew: “you.” The Hebrew switches between “you” and “it.”
Hebrew: “all that drink water.”
Sheol is the place of the dead. The name is also used in verses 16 and 17.
Or “I covered the deep over it.” The Hebrew is hard to understand. The Septuagint says only that the deep mourned.
The Hebrew is hard to understand. The Septuagint says “his offspring.”
To be uncircumcised among the dead meant a shameful death, with no honor.

subheads.1: The Great Cedar Is Cut Down

verses.text: On the first day of the twelfth month (in February–March) of the twelfth year,{a} Yahweh spoke to me:

“Mortal one, sing a funeral song for Pharaoh, king of Egypt. Say to him:
Among the nations you pictured yourself as a young lion.
In truth you are a sea monster.
You splash through your rivers,
stir the water with your feet,
and make the streams muddy.

“The Lord Yahweh says:
I will throw My net over you,
and a crowd of many nations
will drag you up in My big net.

I will toss you on dry land
and hurl you down in an open field.
Birds of every kind will settle on you,
and the beasts of the whole world will stuff themselves with your flesh.

I will pile your meat on the mountains
and fill the valleys with your bones.{b}

I will soak the land with your blood,
all the way to the hills,
and the gullies will be full of you.

When I snuff out your light, I will cover the sky
and turn its stars dark.
The sun will vanish behind clouds,
and the moon will not shine.

I will darken every bright light in the sky
above you,
and I will spread darkness over your land,
says the Lord Yahweh.

“I will upset the hearts of many peoples
when I carry you off as a captive{c} among the nations,
to lands you never knew.

Many peoples will be shocked at you.
Their kings will shake with terror over you
when My sword flashes in front of them.
On the day you fall,
each one will tremble every moment for his own life.

“The Lord Yahweh says:
The sword of the king of Babylon
is coming at you.

I will make your crowds fall
by the swords of mighty soldiers,
the cruelest of all nations.
They will wreck Egypt’s pride,
and all her crowds will be destroyed.

I will wipe out all her cattle
that graze by the great waters.
No human foot will muddy the water again,
and no animal’s hoof will muddy it.

Then I will let the water settle,
and her rivers will run smooth as oil,
says the Lord Yahweh.

I will turn Egypt into an empty waste,
stripped of everything it held.
I will strike down all who live there,
and they will know that I am Yahweh.

This is a funeral song, and it will be sung.
The daughters of the nations will sing it.
Over Egypt and her many people they will chant,
says the Lord Yahweh.”
In the twelfth year, on the fifteenth day of the month,{d} Yahweh spoke to me:
“Mortal one, cry over Egypt’s crowd. Send Egypt down to the world below, together with the daughters of the mighty nations, to join those who go down into the pit.
Ask them, ‘Are you prettier than anyone else? Go down and lie with the people who were never circumcised!’{e}
Egypt will fall among those who died in battle. A sword is ready. Drag her away with all her crowds.{f}
From inside Sheol the greatest of the strong ones will call out to Pharaoh and his helpers: ‘The people who were never circumcised have come down. Cut down by swords, they lie still.’
“Assyria is there with her whole army. Their graves circle her,{g} and every one of them was struck down in battle.
Her graves are in the deepest part of the pit, and her army lies all around her grave. Every one of them fell in battle. They once made people in the land of the living afraid.

“Elam{h} is there too, with her crowd around her grave. Every one of them fell in battle. They went down to the world below without being circumcised. They once filled the land of the living with fear, but now they carry their shame down to the pit with the others.

They made a bed for her among the dead, with all her crowd around it. Their graves circle her. None were ever circumcised, and the sword killed them all. They once spread fear in the land of the living, so now they carry their shame with those in the pit. She lies among the dead.
“Meshech and Tubal{i} are there with all their crowds, and their graves circle them. None were ever circumcised, and the sword ran them through, because they spread fear in the land of the living.

They do not lie with the fallen heroes of long ago, who were also never circumcised.{j} Those heroes went down to Sheol with their weapons. Their swords were under their heads, and their shields{k} covered their bones. They too had made the strong afraid in the land of the living.
And you, Pharaoh, will be broken among people who were never circumcised. You will lie next to the dead of the battlefield.

“Edom is there, with her kings and every one of her princes. They were mighty, but now they lie beside soldiers who were cut down. They lie with the people who were never circumcised and with all who went down to the pit.

“Every prince of the north is there, and so are the people of Sidon. They went down in shame with the dead, though their power once filled people with fear. They lie among those who were never circumcised, slain in war. They bear their shame with those in the pit.
“Pharaoh will see them, and he will find comfort about his many people. Pharaoh and his whole army died in battle, says the Lord Yahweh.

I let people fear him{l} in the land of the living. Yet he will be laid among those who were never circumcised, beside those who died in war. Pharaoh and all his crowds will lie there, says the Lord Yahweh.”

notes.text: Hebrew: “in the twelfth year, in the twelfth month, on the first of the month.” The year counts from spring, so this date is about March 585 BC.
Or “the pile of worms.” The Hebrew word is uncertain.
This follows the Hebrew. The Septuagint says “your captivity.”
The Hebrew does not name the month. It may be the twelfth month of verse 1, which would be about March 585 BC.
The Septuagint does not have this verse. It has a different order for verses 19 to 21.
The Hebrew of this verse is hard to understand.
Hebrew: “him.” The Hebrew switches between “he” and “she” for Assyria in verses 22 to 25.
Elam was a kingdom east of Babylon, in what is now southwest Iran.
On Meshech and Tubal, see the note at 27:13.
The Septuagint says “with the giants who fell long ago.” It may have read the Hebrew word a little differently.
This follows a likely reading. The Hebrew says “their sins.”
This follows the Hebrew text and the Septuagint. The Hebrew margin says “My terror.”

subheads.17: Egypt Goes Down to the Dead

verses.text: Yahweh spoke to me:
“Mortal one, speak to your people. Tell them this: A land faces an enemy army that I have sent. The citizens select one man from among them and post him as a guard.
He sees the army coming. He blows the ram’s horn{a} and warns the people.
Then someone hears the horn but ignores it. The army arrives and kills him. His death is his own fault.
The horn sounded, yet he took no notice. His own life is on his own hands. Had he paid attention, he would have escaped.

But suppose the watchman sees the army coming and never blows the horn. The people have no warning, and the enemy kills one of them. That person dies in his own sin, but I will blame the watchman for his death.
“Mortal one, I have made you a watchman for Israel’s people. When you hear a message from Me, give them My warning.
Suppose I say to a wicked man, ‘You will die,’ and you do not speak up to turn him from his ways. That wicked man will die in his sin, but I will blame you for his death.
But if you do warn him and he still will not turn, then his sin will be the cause of his death. You, though, will have saved yourself.
“Mortal one, tell Israel’s people what they are saying: ‘Our sins and rebellion weigh us down. We are rotting away under them. How can we stay alive?’

Tell them: By My life, says the Lord Yahweh, the death of a wicked person gives Me no pleasure. What I want is for the wicked to change their ways and live. Turn back! Leave your evil ways! People of Israel, why choose to die?

“Mortal one, tell your people: A good man’s goodness will not rescue him on the day he rebels. A wicked man’s evil will not bring him down on the day he turns away from it. A good man cannot stay alive because of his past goodness if he sins.
Suppose I promise a good man that he will live, but he leans on his own goodness and then does wrong. All his good deeds will be forgotten, and he will die in the wrong he has done.
Or suppose I tell a wicked man, ‘You will die,’ but he quits sinning and begins to do what is just and right.
He returns the item a borrower left with him as a guarantee. He repays the money he took. He lives by the laws that give life, and he does no wrong. That man will live. He will not die.
None of his sins will be held against him. He has done what is fair and right, and he will live.
“Yet your people say, ‘The Lord’s way is unfair.’ But their own way is the one that is unfair.
When a good man turns from his goodness and does evil, he will die for it.
And when a wicked man quits his evil and does what is just and right, that is why he will live.
Still you say, ‘The Lord’s way is unfair.’ People of Israel, each of you will be judged by your own way of living.”
In the twelfth year since we were taken away, on the fifth day of the tenth month (in December–January),{b} a survivor from Jerusalem reached me with news: “The city has been struck down!”
The evening before he came, Yahweh’s hand had touched me. By the time the man reached me in the morning, Yahweh had opened my mouth. I could speak again, and I was silent no more.
Yahweh spoke to me:
“Mortal one, the people living in the ruins in Israel’s land are saying, ‘Abraham was just one man, and he got the whole land. There are many of us. Surely the land is ours to keep.’
So tell them: The Lord Yahweh says: Bloody meat is on your tables. You look up to your idols. You spill blood. Do you think the land will be yours?
You trust in your swords. You do disgusting things. Every one of you makes his neighbor’s wife unclean. Do you think the land will be yours?{c}

“Tell them: The Lord Yahweh says: As surely as I live, the people in the ruins will die in battle. I will give those out in the open to wild animals to eat. Those in forts and caves will die of sickness.
I will turn the land into a wasteland that shocks everyone. Its proud strength will end. The mountains of Israel will be so empty that no one will walk through them.
When I turn the land into a shocking wasteland because of all their disgusting acts, they will know that I am Yahweh.
“Mortal one, your own people gossip about you by the walls and at their doorways. They tell each other, ‘Come on, let’s go hear what message has come from Yahweh.’

They come to you in a crowd, the way people do. They sit down before you and act like My people. They listen to what you say, yet they will not obey. Sweet words pour from their mouths,{d} but their hearts chase after money.
To them you are only an entertainer, a man with a lovely voice who sings romantic songs and plays well. They hear what you say, but none of them acts on it.
But it is coming. When it happens, they will realize that a prophet was among them.”

notes.text: Hebrew: shofar. The word is also used in verses 4 to 6.
Hebrew: “in the twelfth year of our exile, in the tenth month, on the fifth of the month.” The year counts from spring, so this date is about January 585 BC.
The Septuagint does not have most of verses 25 and 26.
Or “they act out of lust.” The Hebrew is uncertain. The Septuagint says “lies are in their mouths.”

verses.text: Yahweh spoke to me:

“Mortal one, speak against the shepherds of Israel. Give this message to the shepherds: The Lord Yahweh says: How terrible for the shepherds of Israel, who feed only themselves! Is a shepherd not supposed to feed the flock?
Milk{a} is your drink, and wool is your clothing. You butcher the fattest animals. Yet you never feed the flock.
The weak sheep got no strength from you. You did not heal the sick or wrap the hurt ones. The runaways stayed away, and the lost ones stayed lost. You ruled them with harsh and cruel force.
So the sheep scattered because they had no shepherd, and wild animals ate them.
My sheep wandered across every mountain and tall hill. Over the whole earth they were scattered, and no one went to look for them.
“So, shepherds, hear the word of Yahweh.

As surely as I live, says the Lord Yahweh, My sheep have become loot. With no shepherd, they became meals for wild animals. My shepherds never went out searching. They fed themselves and left My flock hungry.
So hear this, you shepherds. It is a word from Yahweh.

Here is what the Lord Yahweh says: Look, the shepherds are My enemies! I will take My flock out of their care. They will stop being shepherds of the flock, and they will stop feeding themselves. I will pull My sheep from their mouths, and the sheep will not be their food anymore.
“The Lord Yahweh says: I Myself will go out and search for My sheep. I will tend them.

When a shepherd’s sheep are scattered and mixed up around him, he goes to look for them. That is how I will look for My sheep. I will pull them back from every place where they were scattered on that day of clouds and darkness.

I will bring them away from the peoples and collect them from the countries. I will lead them into their own land. They will eat on the mountains of Israel, along the streams, and in every settled place.
I will give them good grass, and their pasture will be the high mountains of Israel. They will rest in a good sheepfold there, and they will graze on rich grass on those mountains.
I Myself will shepherd My sheep. I Myself will make them lie down in peace, says the Lord Yahweh.
I will hunt for the lost sheep and return the runaways. I will bandage the hurt and give strength to the weak. The fat and strong sheep I will wipe out.{b} I will feed My flock with justice.
“As for you, My flock, this is the word of the Lord Yahweh: I am going to judge each sheep, and I will separate the rams from the goats.
It is not enough for you to graze on the best grass. Must you also stomp on what is left? You drink clear water, but must you also muddy what is left with your feet?
My other sheep have to eat the grass you trampled and drink the water you stirred up.
“So the Lord Yahweh tells them: I will now settle the case between the plump sheep and the skinny sheep.
You shove the weak ones with your sides and shoulders. You jab them with your horns until they are chased far away.
So I will rescue My flock, and they will never be loot again. I will judge between one sheep and another.
Over them I will place a single shepherd, My servant David. He will feed them himself, and he will be their shepherd.
I, Yahweh, will be their God. My servant David will be a prince among them. I, Yahweh, have given My word.
“I will make a promise of peace to them.{c} I will chase the wild animals from the land. My flock will rest in the open desert and sleep in the woods without fear.
I will make them and the places around My hill a blessing.{d} Rain will fall in its season, showers that bless them.

The trees in the fields will bear fruit, and the earth will give its crops. My people will be safe on their own soil. I will snap the bars of their yoke and set them free from their slave masters, and then they will know that I am Yahweh.
The nations will never again plunder them. Wild animals will not devour them. They will rest safely, and nobody will frighten them.
I will give them a field of crops that is known far and wide.{e} Hunger will not sweep them away in the land, and the nations will not mock them again.
By then they will see that I am with them. I, Yahweh, am their God. They are the people of Israel, and they belong to Me, says the Lord Yahweh.
You are My sheep, the flock I feed. You are human,{f} and I am your God, says the Lord Yahweh.”

notes.text: This follows the Hebrew vowels. With other vowels, and in the Septuagint, it says “the milk.” The Hebrew word means “fat.”
This follows the Hebrew. The Septuagint says “I will guard the strong,” which comes from a similar Hebrew word.
Hebrew: “cut a covenant of peace.”
Or “I will make them a blessing around My hill.” The Septuagint says “I will settle them around My mountain.”
Hebrew: “a planting for a name.” The Septuagint says “a plant of peace.”
Hebrew: adam, which means “humankind.” It is the same word as in “son of man,” which means “mortal one” in this book.

verses.text: Yahweh spoke to me:
“Mortal one, face Mount Seir{a} and speak against it.
Tell it: The Lord Yahweh says: Mount Seir, I am your enemy. I will raise My hand against you and leave you a wasteland.
I will turn your towns to rubble. You will be a desert, and you will learn that I am Yahweh.
You held a hatred that never died. When Israel’s people were in trouble, at the hour of their final punishment, you handed them over to the sword.
So I swear by My life, says the Lord Yahweh, that I will give you over to bloodshed, and it will chase you down. You did not hate to spill blood, so blood will chase you.{b}
I will make Mount Seir a shocking wasteland. I will cut off everyone who comes and goes there.
I will cover your mountains with dead bodies. People killed in battle will lie on your hills, in your valleys, and in all your gullies.
I will make you a desert forever. Your towns will stand empty.{c} By this you will learn that I am Yahweh.
You said, ‘Both these nations and both these lands belong to us now. We will seize them.’ But Yahweh was there.
So I swear by My life, says the Lord Yahweh, that I will pay you back for the anger and jealousy your hatred showed. I will make Myself known among My people{d} when I judge you.
Then you will learn that I am Yahweh. I heard every insult you hurled at the mountains of Israel. You said, ‘They are ruined! They were handed to us to swallow up.’
You bragged against Me with your own mouths. You piled up words against Me, and I heard them.
The Lord Yahweh says: While the whole earth celebrates, I will leave you in ruins.

You were glad when Israel’s land became a wasteland. I will do the same to you. You will be a wasteland, Mount Seir, and all of Edom with you, from edge to edge. Then everyone will learn that I am Yahweh.”

notes.text: See the note at 25:8.
The Hebrew of this verse is hard to understand. The word for “blood” may also hint at the name Edom, which sounds like the Hebrew word for “blood.”
This follows the Hebrew margin. The main Hebrew text may be read “will not return.”
Hebrew: “among them.” The Septuagint says “to you.”

verses.text: “Mortal one, speak to the mountains of Israel. Tell them: Mountains of Israel, listen to a message from Yahweh.
The Lord Yahweh says: Your enemy laughed at you and said, ‘Ha! The ancient hills{a} now belong to us!’
So give them this message. The Lord Yahweh says: They wrecked you and attacked you from every side. Then the other nations took you for their own, and people whispered and gossiped about you.

So listen, mountains of Israel, to the word of the Lord Yahweh. He speaks to the mountains and hills, to the gullies and valleys, to the empty ruins and lonely cities. The nations all around robbed them and laughed at them. This is what the Lord Yahweh tells them:

My jealous love burns, and I have spoken against the other nations and against all of Edom. They took My land for themselves and were glad about it with scorn in their hearts. They wanted to drive out its people and loot its pastures.{b}
So speak about the land of Israel. Tell the mountains, hills, gullies, and valleys: The Lord Yahweh says: I speak in My burning jealousy and anger, because you have suffered the nations’ insults.
So the Lord Yahweh says: I raise My hand and promise that the nations around you will suffer insults of their own.
“But you, mountains of Israel, will put out new branches and bear fruit for My people Israel. They will soon be home.
I care about you. I will turn to you, and people will plow your soil and plant seed.
I will fill you with people, with all of Israel’s people. The towns will have people in them again, and the ruins will be rebuilt.

I will fill you with people and animals. They will have many young and grow in number. You will be settled as in earlier days, and I will do better for you than before. Then you will learn that I am Yahweh.
I will bring My people Israel to walk across you. You will be their own inheritance, and you will not rob them of children again.
“The Lord Yahweh says: People tell you, ‘You eat up your own people and make your nation lose its children.’
But you will never eat up people again or rob your nation{c} of its children, says the Lord Yahweh.
I will not let you hear the nations’ mocking again. You will not carry the insults of the peoples any longer. Your nation will not stumble{d} because of you, says the Lord Yahweh.”
Yahweh spoke to me:
“Mortal one, when Israel’s people lived in their own land, they made it unclean by the way they lived and what they did. In My eyes their ways were as unclean as a woman during her monthly time.
So I poured out My anger on them, because they had spilled blood in the land and made it filthy with idols.
I scattered them among the nations and spread them across the countries. I judged them by how they lived and what they did.
Wherever they went among the nations, they shamed My holy name. People said about them, ‘These are Yahweh’s people, and yet they had to leave His land.’
I cared about My holy name, which Israel’s people dishonored among the nations where they went.
“So tell Israel’s people: The Lord Yahweh says: People of Israel, I am not acting for your sake. I am acting for My holy name, which you dishonored among the nations where you went.

I will prove that My great name is holy. You made it look cheap among the nations, but I will make it honored again. The nations will know that I am Yahweh when I show My holiness through you as they watch, says the Lord Yahweh.{e}
“I will take you from among the peoples. From every country I will gather you, and I will lead you home to your own soil.
Clean water will be sprinkled over you by Me, and you will be clean. I will wash away everything that made you unclean, and I will wash you clean of all your idols.
I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit in you. The heart of stone will come out of your chest, and I will give you a heart of flesh in its place.
I will place My Spirit{f} inside you. I will help you to live by My laws, and you will carefully obey My rules.
Your home will be the land I gave to your ancestors. I will be your God, and My people is what you will be.
I will rescue you from everything that makes you unclean. I will call for the grain and make it grow plentiful, and I will not bring hunger on you.
I will give you more fruit on the trees and more crops in the fields. Then the nations will never again shame you because of hunger.
Then you will think back on your evil ways and your bad deeds. You will be disgusted with yourselves for your sins and your disgusting acts.
Do not think I am doing this for your sake, says the Lord Yahweh. Make no mistake about that. People of Israel, be ashamed and embarrassed about the way you lived.
“The Lord Yahweh says: On the day I clean away all your sins, I will fill your towns with people again, and the ruins will be rebuilt.
The empty land will be farmed, though everyone who walked by used to see it lying in ruins.
They will say, ‘This land that was empty is now like the garden of Eden. The towns that were wrecked, empty, and torn down now have walls and people.’
Then the nations still around you will know that I, Yahweh, rebuilt what was torn down and planted what was empty. I, Yahweh, have spoken, and I will do it.
“The Lord Yahweh says: Once more I will let Israel’s people ask Me for this, and I will do it for them. Their numbers will swell like a flock.

Think of the flocks brought for sacrifice, the flocks that filled Jerusalem at her special feasts. In the same way, the ruined towns will fill up with flocks of people. That is how they will find out that I am Yahweh.”

notes.text: Or “the everlasting hilltops.”
The Hebrew of the last part of this verse is hard to understand.
This follows the Hebrew margin and the Septuagint. The Hebrew text says “make your nation fall.”
The Septuagint does not have this line.
Papyrus 967, one of the oldest Greek copies of Ezekiel (about AD 200), is reported to have this verse in a different place. Some other ancient copies do not have the end of the verse.
Or “My spirit.” The Hebrew word ruach also means “wind” or “breath.” See 37:1–14.

subheads.1: Good News for the Mountains of Israel
subheads.22: A New Heart and a New Spirit

verses.text: The hand of Yahweh came upon me. Through Yahweh’s Spirit{a} I was lifted up and placed in the center of a valley.{b} Bones covered the ground.
Yahweh walked me around them in every direction. There were more bones than I could count lying across the valley floor, and every one was bone dry.
“Mortal one,” He asked, “can these bones come back to life?” I answered, “Lord Yahweh, You are the only one who knows.”
Then He told me, “Announce My word to these bones: Dry bones, listen to Yahweh’s message!
This is what the Lord Yahweh says to you, bones: I am sending breath{c} into you, and life will be yours.
Muscles will grow on you, and flesh will cover you. Skin will stretch over you, and breath will fill you. You will come alive, and you will know that I am Yahweh.”
I did what He commanded, and as I spoke, a noise began. It was a rattle. Bones moved together, each one joining its partner.
While I watched, muscles formed on the bones. Flesh grew, and skin spread over it. But the bodies lay without breath.
Next He told me, “Call out to the breath. Mortal one, say to the breath: The Lord Yahweh says: Come from all four winds, breath! Blow on these dead bodies, and let them live!”
I did what He commanded. Breath came into the bodies, and they lived. They stood up, a very large army.
He said to me, “Mortal one, all the people of Israel are these bones. They say, ‘Our bones have dried up. Hope is gone. We are cut off.’
So give them My message: The Lord Yahweh says: My people, I will open up your graves and lift you out. I will bring you back to Israel’s soil.
My people, you will know that I am Yahweh when I open your graves and lift you out of them.
My Spirit will enter you, and life will be yours. I will place you in your own land. You will know that I, Yahweh, have spoken, and that I have done what I said, says Yahweh.”
Yahweh spoke to me:

“Mortal one, take a stick.{d} Write on it, ‘This belongs to Judah and the Israelites joined with him.’ Take another stick and write on it, ‘This belongs to Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and all the people of Israel joined with him.’
Join them end to end, so that they are one stick in your hand.
When your people ask, ‘What do these sticks mean? Will you explain them to us?’

tell them what the Lord Yahweh says: I will pick up Joseph’s stick. It is in Ephraim’s hand, along with the tribes of Israel that belong to him. I will lay Judah’s stick beside it and make one stick of both. In My hand they will be a single piece.{e}
Hold the sticks you wrote on up in front of their eyes.
Then tell them: The Lord Yahweh says: I will pick up the Israelites from the nations where they have gone. From every side I will gather them and lead them back to their own country.
In that country, on the mountains of Israel, I will make them a single nation. A single king will rule over all of them. Never again will they be two nations or two separate kingdoms.

Idols, disgusting statues, and sins of every kind will never make them unclean again. I will save them from all the unfaithful ways that led them to sin,{f} and I will wash them clean. They will be My people, and I will be their God.
“My servant David will be their king, and one shepherd will lead them all. They will follow My rules and keep My laws with care.

They will settle in the land I gave My servant Jacob, where your ancestors lived. They and their children and grandchildren will stay there forever. David, My servant, will be their prince for all time.
I will make a promise of peace with them, a promise that never ends. I will settle them, make their numbers grow,{g} and set My holy place among them for all time.
Among them I will make My home. I will be their God, and they will be My people.
When My holy place stands among them forever, the nations will see that I, Yahweh, make Israel holy.”

verses.text: Yahweh spoke to me:
“Mortal one, face Gog,{a} who comes from the land of Magog.{b} Meshech and Tubal have him as their top prince.{c} Speak against him.
Tell him: The Lord Yahweh says: Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, I am against you.

I will turn you around and hook your jaws. I will drag you out with your whole army, with horses and riders, all in fine gear. It is a great mass of soldiers with big and small shields, and every one of them carries a sword.
Persia, Cush, and Put{d} are in their ranks, and each soldier has a shield and a helmet.
Gomer is there with all its troops. From the far north comes Beth-togarmah,{e} with all of its troops as well. Many peoples march with you.
“Get ready! Prepare yourself, you and all the armies gathered around you. Be their commander.{f}

After a long time, you will be summoned.{g} In years to come you will invade a land that has recovered from war. Its people were gathered from many nations to the mountains of Israel, which had lain in ruins for a long time. They had been led out of the nations, and they all live in safety now.
You will rush in like a storm. You will cover the land like a cloud, you and all your soldiers and the many peoples with you.
“The Lord Yahweh says: When that day comes, plans will fill your mind. You will think up an evil scheme.
You will say, ‘I will march on a land of villages without walls. I will go after quiet people who feel safe. None of them has a wall, a bar, or a gate.’

You will want to grab loot and carry off treasure. You will strike ruins that have people again, and a people gathered from the nations. They are gaining herds and goods, and they live at the very center{h} of the world.

Traders from Sheba, Dedan, and Tarshish,{i} with all its young lions,{j} will question you: ‘Is it loot you came for? Did you gather your army to carry off treasure, to take silver and gold, to snatch herds and goods, and to seize huge piles of loot?’
“So speak out, mortal one, and tell Gog: The Lord Yahweh says: On that day, when My people Israel live in safety, you will notice them,{k} will you not?
Your home is in the far north, and you will leave it. Many nations will come with you, all riding horses, a giant crowd and a strong army.

Like a cloud over the ground, you will roll over My people Israel. In days to come, I will bring you to My land. Then the nations will know Me, because they will watch Me show My holiness through you, Gog.
“The Lord Yahweh says: Are you the one I told about long ago, using My servants, the prophets of Israel? In those days they said for years that I would bring you against Israel.
On the day Gog attacks the land of Israel, says the Lord Yahweh, My anger will blaze up.
In My jealousy and burning rage I say this: On that day a mighty earthquake will shake the land of Israel.

Sea creatures, birds, and wild animals will tremble before Me. So will all the little things that creep on the ground, and every person on earth. Mountains will topple, steep cliffs{l} will crumble, and each wall will fall flat.
I will call for a sword against Gog on all My mountains,{m} says the Lord Yahweh. Each man’s sword will strike his own brother.
I will judge him with sickness and bloodshed. Flooding rain, hailstones, fire, and burning sulfur will pour down on him, on his troops, and on the many peoples with him.
In this way I will show how great and holy I am. Many nations will watch, and they will learn that I am Yahweh.”

Or “the prince of Rosh.” The Hebrew is nesi rosh. The Septuagint takes Rosh as a name. Others take it to mean “chief.”
Cush was the upper Nile region, south of Egypt. Put is probably Libya.
Gomer was probably the Cimmerians. Beth-togarmah was a land in eastern Asia Minor.

verses.text: “Mortal one, speak against Gog. Say: The Lord Yahweh says: Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, I am against you.
I will spin you around and drag you along.{a} I will pull you from the far north and bring you to the mountains of Israel.
Your bow will be knocked out of your left hand, and your arrows will be shaken from your right. Then you will drop dead on the mountains of Israel.
You will fall on the mountains of Israel, you and all your soldiers and the nations with you. Every bird that eats dead flesh and every wild animal will get you as food.
You will fall in the open country. I have given My word, says the Lord Yahweh.
I will send fire on Magog{b} and on those who live without a care along the coasts. By this they will learn that I am Yahweh.
“I will make My holy name known among My people Israel. I will not allow it to be shamed again. Then the nations will see that I am Yahweh, Israel’s Holy One.
It is coming, and it will surely happen, says the Lord Yahweh. That is the day I told you about.

“Then the people from Israel’s towns will walk out and light fires with the weapons. Small shields, large shields, bows, arrows, clubs, and spears will all go into the flames. For seven years the fires will burn.

They will not need to gather wood in the fields or cut it in the forests, because the weapons will be their fuel. They will take the goods of those who took theirs, and loot those who looted them, says the Lord Yahweh.

“That same day I will give Gog a burial ground in Israel. It is the Valley of the Travelers,{c} east of the Sea.{d} Gog and his whole army will be buried there, and the grave will block travelers on their road. The place will be known as the Valley of Hamon-gog.{e}
Burying them and making the land clean will take Israel’s people seven months.
All the people of the land will help with the burying. The day I show My glory will bring them fame, declares the Lord Yahweh.
They will choose men to work full time, walking through the land to bury the bodies{f} still lying on the ground. They will make the land clean. At the end of seven months they will begin to search.
As they walk through the land, anyone who sees a human bone will set up a marker beside it. It will stay there until the gravediggers carry it to the Valley of Hamon-gog.
A city there will be named Hamonah.{g} So the land will be made clean.

“As for you, mortal one, the Lord Yahweh says: Call every bird and wild animal of every kind. Tell them: Gather and come! Come together from every side to the great feast I am preparing for you. It is a huge sacrifice on the Israelite mountains. There you will eat meat and drink blood.
You will devour the bodies of fighting men and drink the blood of the world’s rulers. They are like rams, lambs, goats, and bulls, all fattened in Bashan.{h}
At the feast I am preparing, you will gorge on fat until you are full, and you will drink blood until you stagger.
My table will be piled high with horses and riders,{i} with soldiers and fighters of every kind, says the Lord Yahweh.
“I will show My glory to the nations. All of them will see how I judge and how My hand came down on them.
From then on, Israel’s people will know that I am Yahweh their God.

The nations will also understand that Israel’s people were taken away because of their sin. They had been unfaithful to Me. For that reason My face was hidden from them. I gave them to their enemies, and all of them died in battle.
I treated them as their filthy ways and their rebellion deserved, and I turned My face away from them.
“So the Lord Yahweh says: Now I will bring Jacob’s people back from captivity.{j} I will have mercy on every person in Israel, and I will fiercely defend My holy name.
They will forget{k} their shame and every act of unfaithfulness toward Me. They will live safely in their own land, and no one will scare them.
I will bring them home from the peoples and gather them from their enemies’ lands. Through them I will show My holiness while many nations watch.
Then they will know that I am Yahweh their God. I sent them away to live among the nations, and then I gathered them to their own land. Not one of them will stay behind.{l}
I will never again turn My face away from them. I will have poured My Spirit out over Israel’s people, says the Lord Yahweh.”
