verses.text: It was the twenty-fifth year since we were taken away, at the start of the year, on the tenth day of the month.{a} Fourteen years had passed since the city fell. Yahweh’s hand came on me that same day, and He carried me there.
In visions from God He took me to the land of Israel. He placed me on a very tall mountain. On its southern slope stood a group of buildings that looked like a town.{b}
He led me up close, and I saw a man whose body shone like bronze. In a gateway he stood holding a linen cord and a measuring rod.
The man told me, “Mortal one, look carefully and listen well. Fix your mind on all that I show you. This is why you were brought here. Report everything you see to the people of Israel.”

A wall ran all the way around the temple grounds.{c} The man held a measuring rod that was 10.5 feet long. Each unit in it was a long cubit, which is a cubit plus a handbreadth.{d} He measured the wall. It was 10.5 feet thick and 10.5 feet high.{e}
He walked to the east gate and climbed its steps. There he measured the doorway{f} of the gate, and it was 10.5 feet deep.{g}
Each guard room{h} was 10.5 feet long and 10.5 feet wide. The walls between the guard rooms were 8.75 feet thick. The doorway of the gate next to the porch, on the inside, was 10.5 feet deep.{i}
Next he measured the gate’s inner porch. It was 10.5 feet deep.{j}{k}
Then he measured the gate’s porch. It was 14 feet across, and its side posts{l} were 3.5 feet thick.{m} That porch opened toward the inside.
The east gate had three guard rooms on each side. All three were the same size, and the side posts on each side were the same size too.
He measured the opening of the gateway. It was 17.5 feet wide and about 23 feet long.{n}
A low wall 21 inches wide stood in front of the guard rooms on each side. The guard rooms were 10.5 feet square.{o}
Next he measured the gate from the back wall{p} of one guard room to the back wall of the opposite room. The distance was about 44 feet,{q} from one door to the door across from it.
He also measured the side posts,{r} which came to 105 feet.{s} The courtyard reached out to the side posts all around the gateway.
From the front of the outer entrance to the front of the inner porch was 87.5 feet.{t}
The guard rooms, their side posts, and the porch had narrow windows{u} all around, facing the inside of the gateway. Palm trees were carved on each side post.
Then he took me into the outer courtyard. A stone pavement ran all around it, and thirty rooms stood along the pavement.
The pavement ran along the sides of the gates, as long as the gates were. This was the lower pavement.
He measured the space between the front of the lower gate and the front of the inner courtyard, on the outside. It was 175 feet,{v} on the east side and on the north side.{w}
Next he measured the gate on the north side of the outer courtyard, both its length and its width.
It had three guard rooms on each side, with side posts and a porch. All of them were the same size as the first gate. The gate was 87.5 feet long and about 44 feet wide.{x}
Its windows, porch, and palm carvings matched those of the gate on the east. A flight of seven steps went up to it, and its porch opened toward the inside.
Across from the north gate, as on the east side, was a gate to the inner courtyard. He measured from gate to gate, and it was 175 feet.{y}
Then he led me to the south side. There was a gate facing south. He measured its posts and its porch, and they were the same as the others.
Windows ran all around the gate and its porch, like the windows of the other gates. The gate was 87.5 feet long and about 44 feet wide.{z}
Seven steps led up to it, and its porch faced the inside. Palm trees were carved on its side posts, one on each side.
The inner courtyard also had a gate facing south. He measured from that gate to the south gate of the outer courtyard, and it was 175 feet.{aa}
Then he led me into the inner courtyard by the south gate. He measured that gate, and its size matched the others.
Its guard rooms, side posts, and porch were the same size as the others, and windows ran all around it and its porch. It was 87.5 feet long and about 44 feet wide.{ab}
Porches ran all around. They were about 44 feet long and 8.75 feet wide.{ac}{ad}
Its porch opened toward the outer courtyard. Carved palm trees decorated its side posts, and a stairway of eight steps led up to it.
Then he led me into the inner courtyard on its eastern side and measured that gate. Its size matched the others.
Its guard rooms, side posts, and porch had the same size as the others, and windows ran all around it and its porch. Its length was 87.5 feet, and its width was about 44 feet.{ae}
Its porch opened toward the outer courtyard. Carved palm trees decorated the side posts on both sides, and eight steps led up to it.
Then he led me to the north gate and measured it. Its size was the same as the rest.
Its guard rooms, side posts, and porch matched too, and windows ran all around. It was 87.5 feet long and about 44 feet wide.{af}
Its side posts{ag} opened toward the outer courtyard. Carved palm trees decorated the side posts on both sides, and a stairway of eight steps led up to it.
A room with a door stood by the side posts of the gates.{ah} There the priests rinsed the animals for the burnt offering.
Two tables stood on each side inside the gate’s porch. On them the priests killed the animals for the burnt offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering.
Two tables stood on the outer side of the porch, near the steps up to the north gate. Two more stood on the other side of the gate’s porch.
Four tables stood on one side of the gate and four on the other. That made eight tables for killing the animals.

Four more tables, cut from stone, were for the burnt offering. Each was 31.5 inches long, 31.5 inches wide, and 21 inches high.{ai} The priests laid on them the tools for killing the animals for burnt offerings and other sacrifices.
Hooks{aj} 3 inches long were fixed to the walls all around inside,{ak} and the meat of the offerings was laid on the tables.

Two rooms for the singers{al} stood in the inner courtyard, just outside the inner gate. The first stood next to the north gate, looking south. The second stood next to the south{am} gate, looking north.
The man told me, “The room facing south belongs to the priests who watch over the temple.
The room facing north belongs to the priests who watch over the altar. They are descendants of Zadok.{an} Of all the descendants of Levi, only they may come near to Yahweh to serve Him.”
He measured the courtyard. It formed a square with sides of 175 feet.{ao} In front of the temple stood the altar.
Then he took me to the temple porch. He measured the side posts of the porch, and each was 8.75 feet thick. The gateway was 24.5 feet wide, and its side walls were 5.25 feet thick.{ap}{aq}
The porch was 35 feet wide{ar} and 21 feet deep.{as}{at} Steps led up to it,{au} and there were pillars by the side posts, one on each side.

verses.text: Then the man led me into the main hall{a} and measured its side posts. Each post was 10.5 feet thick.{b}{c}
The entrance was 17.5 feet wide, and each wall beside it was 8.75 feet thick. He measured the main hall, and its length was 70 feet while its width was 35 feet.{d}
Then he went farther in and measured the posts at the entrance. They were 3.5 feet thick. The doorway was 10.5 feet wide, and the walls beside it were about 12 feet thick.{e}{f}
He measured the room beyond, at the far end of the main hall. Its length was 35 feet and its width was 35 feet.{g} The man told me, “This is the Most Holy Place.”
Next he measured the temple wall. It was 10.5 feet thick. Side rooms ran all around the temple, and each one was 7 feet wide.{h}

The side rooms were stacked in three floors, with thirty rooms on each floor.{i} Ledges stuck out of the temple wall all around, and the beams of the side rooms rested on them. The beams were not set into the temple wall itself.

The side rooms got wider on each higher floor, because the building around the temple went up in steps. So the temple was wider at the top. A stairway went from the bottom floor to the top floor by way of the middle one.{j}
I noticed that the temple sat on a platform that circled it. The platform formed the foundation for the side rooms, and its height was a full rod, 10.5 feet.{k}{l}
The outer wall of the side rooms was 8.75 feet thick.{m} An open space was left between the side rooms of the temple
and the rooms of the priests.{n} That space was 35 feet wide on every side of the temple.{o}
The side rooms had doors that opened onto the open space, one facing north and one facing south. The open space was 8.75 feet wide all the way around.{p}
The building that faced the temple yard{q} on the west side was about 123 feet wide. Its wall was 8.75 feet thick all around, and the building was about 158 feet long.{r}
Then he measured the temple. It was 175 feet long. The yard and the building, with its walls, were also 175 feet long.{s}
The front of the temple, with the yard on its east side, was 175 feet wide.{t}

The main hall, the inner room,{v} and the porches of the courtyard,

The doorways, the narrow windows, and the balconies around all three, across from the doorway, were covered with wood on every side. The wood reached from the floor up to the windows, and the windows had covers too.{w}
up to the space above the door, and into the inner room and outside it. Carvings in even rows{x} covered every wall all around, inside and outside.
They showed winged guardians{y} and palm trees in turn, with a palm tree between each pair of guardians. Each guardian had two faces.
On one side, a person’s face looked toward a palm tree. On the other side, a young lion’s face looked toward the next palm tree. These carvings circled the whole temple.

verses.text: The man took me out to the outer courtyard along the road going north. He brought me to the rooms across from the fenced yard and across from the building on the north side.
The building with the north door{a} was 175 feet long and 87.5 feet wide.{b}
One side faced the 35-foot space{c} that belonged to the inner courtyard. Across from it lay the paved area of the outer courtyard. The balconies looked at each other across three levels.
In front of the rooms was a walkway 17.5 feet wide on the inner side, with a path 21 inches wide beside it.{d}{e} The doors of the rooms faced north.
The rooms on the top floor were narrower, because the balconies took up more of their space than they did on the lower and middle floors.
The rooms were on three floors and had no pillars like those of the courtyards. For that reason each upper floor was set farther back than the one below it.
A wall stood outside, running alongside the rooms toward the outer courtyard. It was 87.5 feet long.{f}
The rooms next to the outer courtyard were 87.5 feet long, but the rooms facing the main hall were 175 feet long.{g}
Below these rooms was an entrance{h} on the east side, where a person comes in from the outer courtyard.
There were also rooms along the thickness of the courtyard wall on the south side,{i} across from the fenced yard and the building.
A walkway ran in front of them. These rooms looked just like the northern ones, with the same length and width. They had the same exits, plans, and doors.
As with the doors of the southern rooms, there was a door where the walkway began, on the path beside the matching wall to the east, where a person enters.{j}

Then he told me, “The north rooms and the south rooms by the fenced yard are holy rooms. The priests who come near to Yahweh will eat the most holy offerings there. They will also set down the most holy offerings there: the grain, the sin offering, and the guilt offering. The place is holy.

When the priests go in, they must not go out of the holy place into the outer courtyard until they take off the clothes they wore to serve. Those clothes are holy. They must change into different clothes before going near the area that belongs to the people.”
After he finished measuring inside the temple, he led me out by way of the east gate. He then measured the whole area around it.
He measured the east side with the measuring rod.{k} It was 5,250 feet by the rod.{l}
He measured the north side. It was also 5,250 feet by the rod.{m}
He measured the south side, and it was 5,250 feet by the rod.{n}
On the west side he did the same, and it was 5,250 feet by the rod.{o}
He measured the area on all four sides. A wall surrounded it, 5,250 feet long and 5,250 feet wide,{p} to keep the holy things apart from the ordinary.

verses.text: The man now walked me over to the gate that looked east.
From the east came the glory of the God of Israel. Its sound roared like many waters,{a} and the earth glowed with His glory.
It matched the vision I saw when I{b} came to destroy the city, and the visions I saw by the Kebar River. I dropped to the ground and pressed my face down.
Through the east gate, the glory of Yahweh entered the temple.
Then the Spirit raised me up and led me into the inner courtyard. And there it was! The glory of Yahweh filled the temple.
Someone spoke to me from inside the temple, and the man was standing by my side.

The voice said, “Mortal one, here is the place for My throne, and here is the place where I rest My feet. Here I will make My home among Israel’s people forever. The people of Israel and their kings will never again make My holy name unclean. They will not be unfaithful to Me, and they will not set up the dead bodies of their kings{c} at their hilltop shrines.{d}

They built their doorway right next to My doorway and their door post beside My door post, with only a wall between us. They made My holy name unclean by the disgusting things they did, so I destroyed them in My anger.
Now let them put their unfaithfulness far away from Me, along with the dead bodies of their kings.{e} Then I will live among them forever.
“Mortal one, describe the temple to the people of Israel. When they see it, they will feel shame for their sins. Have them study its plan.

If they feel shame{f} for all they have done, show them the temple’s design and layout, its exits and entrances, its shapes, and all its rules and teachings. Write them down while they watch, so that they can keep the whole plan and obey all its rules.
This is the law of the temple: On top of the mountain, all the land around the temple is most holy. That is the law of the temple.

“Here are the altar’s sizes, measured in cubits. In this vision a cubit is a cubit plus a handbreadth.{g} A gutter{h} runs around its base. The gutter is 21 inches deep and 21 inches across, and the rim along its edge is 10.5 inches wide.{i} Now this is how tall the altar is:{j}
From the base on the ground to the lower ledge it is 3.5 feet, and the ledge is 21 inches wide. From the smaller ledge to the larger ledge it is 7 feet, and that ledge is also 21 inches wide.{k}
The altar hearth{l} stands 7 feet high,{m} and four horns rise up from it.{n}
The hearth forms a square, 21 feet on each side,{o} so all four sides are equal.
The upper ledge is square too, 24.5 feet long and 24.5 feet wide, with a rim of 10.5 inches all around it and a gutter of 21 inches all around.{p} Its steps face east.”
Then he said to me, “Mortal one, the Lord Yahweh says: These are the rules for the altar on the day it is built, for burning offerings on it and for splashing blood on it.
To the priests from the family of Levi, the descendants of Zadok, who come near to Me to serve Me, you must give a young bull for a sin offering, says the Lord Yahweh.
Take some of its blood and put it on the four horns of the altar, on the four corners of the ledge, and all around the rim. By doing this you will make the altar clean and cover its sin.
Then take the bull of the sin offering and burn it in the place set aside for it in the temple area, outside the holy place.
A male goat with no fault{q} must be offered as a sin offering on the second day. The priests will cleanse the altar, the way they cleansed it with the bull.
When you finish making it clean, bring a young bull with no fault and a ram from the flock with no fault.
Bring them before Yahweh. Salt will be thrown on them by the priests, and the animals will go up in flames as a burnt offering for Yahweh.
For seven days you must prepare one goat each day as a sin offering. A young bull and a ram from the flock, both with no fault, must also be made ready.
For seven days the priests will cover the altar’s sin and make it clean. In this way they will give it to God.{r}
When the seven days are over, the priests will lay your burnt offerings and your peace offerings on the altar, beginning on the eighth day. Then I will accept you, says the Lord Yahweh.”

verses.text: After that, the man turned me around toward the outer gate of the holy place, the one that looks east. It was closed.
Yahweh told me, “Keep this gate closed. Nobody may open it or walk through it, since Yahweh, the God of Israel, has entered through it. So it must be kept closed.
Only the prince{a} is allowed to sit inside the gateway and eat a meal in Yahweh’s presence. He must enter through the porch of the gate and leave by that same route.”
Next the man brought me around to the north gate, facing the temple. I looked up, and Yahweh’s glory was filling Yahweh’s temple! I fell flat on the ground, face down.

Yahweh said, “Mortal one, concentrate. Use your eyes to look and your ears to listen to everything I tell you about the rules and laws of Yahweh’s temple. Take note of who may go into the temple and who must be kept out of the holy place.{b}
Tell the rebellious people,{c} the people of Israel, that the Lord Yahweh says: People of Israel, enough of your disgusting practices!

You brought strangers into My holy place, people whose hearts and bodies were not committed to Me. You made My temple unclean while you offered Me My food, the fat and the blood. Those people{d} broke My agreement, on top of all your other disgusting practices.
My holy things were not guarded by you. Instead you hired others{e} to guard My holy place in your place.
The Lord Yahweh says: No stranger may come into My holy place if his heart and body are not committed to Me. This includes every foreigner who lives among the Israelites.
“The Levites went far from Me when Israel wandered away. They followed their idols{f} and left Me. They will carry the weight of their guilt.

They will serve in My holy place as workers. They will watch over the temple gates and do the work of the temple. They will kill the animals for the burnt offering and for the people’s sacrifices. They will stand before the people and serve them.

These Levites served the people in front of their idols, and they caused Israel’s people to fall into sin. So I have raised My hand and made a vow against them, says the Lord Yahweh. They will carry the weight of their guilt.
They may not come near Me to serve as My priests. They may not touch My holy things or the most holy ones. They must carry their shame and the disgusting things they did.{g}
I will put them in charge of the temple’s daily work, all its jobs and everything that must be done there.

“But the priests from the family of Levi, the descendants of Zadok, kept watch over My holy place while Israel’s people were leaving Me. These priests will come near to serve Me. They will stand before Me and present the fat and the blood, says the Lord Yahweh.
They will go into My holy place. Near My table they will serve Me and carry out My orders.
Whenever they pass through the gates of the inner courtyard, they must dress in linen. No wool may touch them while they serve at those gates or inside the courtyard.
Their turbans will be linen, and their shorts will be linen. Nothing that makes them sweat may be worn.{h}

Suppose the priests go into the outer courtyard, where the people are.{i} Before they do, their serving clothes must come off. They will store those clothes in the holy rooms and put on different clothes. That way, they will not pass holiness to the people through their clothes.
They must not shave their heads or let their hair grow long. Their hair must be cut short.
No priest may drink wine when he goes into the inner courtyard.
They must not marry a widow or a divorced woman. A priest may choose only a young woman who has never been married, from Israel’s people, or a woman whose husband was a priest and has died.{j}
They will teach My people how to tell holy things from ordinary things. They will show them how to know unclean from clean.
If there is a dispute,{k} the priests will stand as judges and decide it by My laws. They will obey My laws and rules at all My special feasts, and they will keep My Sabbaths holy.
No priest may go near a dead body, or he will become unclean. But he may make himself unclean for a father or mother, a son or daughter, a brother, or a sister who has no husband.
When a priest has been made clean, seven days must pass.{l}
Then he may go into the holy place, to the inner courtyard, to serve. On that day he must bring a sin offering for himself, says the Lord Yahweh.
“The priests will have this as their inheritance:{m} I am their inheritance. Give them no land in Israel. I am their share.
The grain offerings, the sin offerings, and the guilt offerings will be their food. Whatever is given to God for good{n} in Israel will be theirs.
The best of all the first harvest and all the special gifts will belong to the priests. You must give the first of your dough{o} to the priest, so that a blessing will rest on your home.
The priests must never eat a bird or animal that died by itself or was torn apart by wild animals.”

subheads.15: Rules for the Priests of Zadok

verses.text: “When you divide the land among the tribes, set aside a holy share for Yahweh. It will be about 8.3 miles long and about 3.3 miles{a} wide.{b} All of it will be holy.{c}
Within it, a square piece 875 feet on each side will belong to the holy place, with a strip of open land 87.5 feet wide all around it.{d}
From the measured area, mark off a strip about 8.3 miles long and about 3.3 miles wide.{e} The holy place, the Most Holy Place, will stand in it.
This is a holy part of the land. It is for the priests who work in the holy place and come near to serve Yahweh. It will give them room for their houses and holy ground for the holy place.
Another strip, about 8.3 miles long and about 3.3 miles wide, will go to the Levites who work in the temple.{f} They will own it as places to live.{g}
“Beside the holy share, give the city its own land, about 1.7 miles wide and about 8.3 miles long.{h} The whole nation of Israel will own it.

The prince will own land on each side of the holy share and the city’s land. It will touch both. On the west it will reach westward, and on the east it will reach eastward. Its length will match one of the tribes’ shares, from the western border to the eastern border.
This land will be the prince’s own property in Israel. My princes will no longer crush My people. They will let the people of Israel have the land by their tribes.
“The Lord Yahweh says: That is enough, princes of Israel! Stop your violence and stealing. Do what is fair and right. Stop forcing My people off their land, says the Lord Yahweh.
Your scales must be honest. So must your dry measure and your liquid measure.{i}
The two measures must be the same size. Each holds one tenth of a homer, and the homer is the standard for both.{j}
A shekel must weigh twenty gerahs, which is about 0.4 ounce. Your mina will be made up of twenty shekels, twenty-five shekels, and fifteen shekels, which is about 1.5 pounds.{k}
“This is the gift you must set aside: one sixtieth of your wheat and one sixtieth of your barley.{l}
The set share of olive oil is one hundredth of it.{m}

Also give one sheep out of every two hundred in Israel’s well-watered pastures.{n} These gifts are for the grain offerings, burnt offerings, and peace offerings, to cover the people’s sin, says the Lord Yahweh.
All the people of the land must join in giving this gift to the prince of Israel.

The prince will be responsible for the burnt offerings, grain offerings, and drink offerings at the festivals, at the new moons, on the Sabbaths, and for every other special feast of Israel. From him will come the sin offerings, grain offerings, burnt offerings, and peace offerings that cover the sin of the people of Israel.
“The Lord Yahweh says: On the first day of the first month (in March–April),{o} take a young bull with no fault and make the holy place clean.
The priest will take blood from the sin offering and smear it on the temple door posts, on the posts of the inner courtyard gate, and on the four corners of the altar’s ledge.
Do the same on the seventh day of the month{p} for anyone who sins by mistake or out of ignorance. In this way you will cover the sin of the temple.
“On the fourteenth day of the first month (in March–April),{q} you will celebrate Passover. It is a feast of seven days,{r} and bread made without yeast must be eaten.
On that day the prince must provide a bull as a sin offering for himself and for everyone in the land.
On each of the seven days of the feast he must give Yahweh a burnt offering of seven bulls and seven rams with no fault. He must also give a male goat each day for a sin offering.
For the grain offering he must provide about 3/5 bushel of flour for each bull and for each ram, with about a gallon of olive oil for each 3/5 bushel.{s}

“The feast begins on the fifteenth day of the seventh month (in September–October).{t} Throughout its seven days he must provide the same kinds of sin offerings, burnt offerings, grain offerings, and oil.”

subheads.1: The Holy Share of the Land

verses.text: “Here is what the Lord Yahweh says: The inner courtyard’s east gate must be kept shut during the six work days. On the Sabbath it must be opened, and it must be opened on the day of the new moon.

The prince will come in from outside through the gate’s porch and stand by the gate post. His burnt offering and peace offerings will be presented by the priests. He will bow down at the gate’s doorway and then go out. But the gate must not be shut until evening.
On the Sabbaths and at the new moons, the people of the land will also bow down before Yahweh at the entrance to that gate.
On the Sabbath the prince will bring Yahweh a burnt offering of six lambs with no fault and a ram with no fault.
With the ram he will bring a grain offering of about 3/5 bushel of flour. With the lambs he will bring whatever grain he wants to give, and about a gallon of olive oil for each 3/5 bushel.{a}
On the day of the new moon he will bring a young bull, six lambs, and a ram, all with no fault.

With the bull he will bring a grain offering of about 3/5 bushel, and the same with the ram. With the lambs he will bring as much as he can afford, with about a gallon of olive oil for each 3/5 bushel.{b}
Whenever the prince enters, he must go in by the porch of the gate, and he must leave the same way.

“When the people of the land come before Yahweh at the special feasts, anyone who comes in by the north gate to worship must leave by the south gate. Anyone who comes in by the south gate must leave by the north gate. Nobody may turn around and leave by the gate he entered. Each person must walk straight ahead.{c}
The prince will be among them. He will go in when they go in and go out when they go out.{d}

At the festivals and special feasts, the grain offering is about 3/5 bushel with a bull and the same with a ram. With the lambs it is whatever he wants to give, with about a gallon of olive oil for each 3/5 bushel.

“Sometimes the prince gives Yahweh a freewill offering, either a burnt offering or a peace offering. Then someone must open the east gate for him. He will bring his burnt offering and peace offering just as he does on the Sabbath. After he walks out, the gate is closed behind him.
“Every day you{e} must bring a one-year-old lamb with no fault as a burnt offering to Yahweh. Bring it every morning.

Every morning you must also bring a grain offering with it. It is about a gallon of flour and about 1.25 quarts of olive oil to mix with the fine flour.{f} This is a grain offering to Yahweh. It is a rule that lasts forever.
So they{g} must bring the lamb, the grain offering, and the oil every morning as a regular burnt offering.
“The Lord Yahweh says: Suppose the prince gives a gift from his own inheritance{h} to one of his sons. It will belong to his sons, and they will keep it as their own inheritance.

But suppose he gives a gift from his inheritance to one of his servants. Only until the year of freedom{i} does it stay with the servant. Then it goes back to the prince. His inheritance belongs only to his sons. It will stay with them.

The prince must not take any of the people’s inheritance and force them off their property. From his own land he must give his sons their inheritance. In this way none of My people will be scattered away from their property.”
Then the man brought me through the entrance beside the gate to the holy rooms that faced north, which belonged to the priests. At the far west end of them I noticed an open area.{j}

He told me, “Here the priests will boil the guilt offering and the sin offering, and here they will bake the grain offering. In this way they will not have to carry them into the outer courtyard and pass holiness to the people.”
After that he took me into the outer courtyard and walked me past its four corners. Each corner held a smaller courtyard.
In all four corners there were walled{k} courtyards, 70 feet long and 52.5 feet wide.{l} All four of the corner courtyards{m} were the same size.
A row of stones ran around the inside of each of the four, and cooking places were built under the rows all around.
He said to me, “These are the kitchens. The temple workers will boil the people’s sacrifices here.”

verses.text: The man brought me back to the entrance of the temple. Water was flowing out from under the temple doorway toward the east, because the temple faced east. The water ran down from under the south side of the temple, south of the altar.
He then led me out of the north gate and around the outer side to the outer gate on the east. A small stream of water was trickling out along the south side.
The man set out eastward, a measuring line in his hand. After 1,750 feet,{a} he had me wade into the water. It reached my ankles.
Another 1,750 feet{b} later he had me wade in again, and the water reached my knees.{c} After 1,750 more feet he had me wade in, and it reached my waist.
After another 1,750 feet, it had become a river I could not cross. The water was too deep for wading. A person would have to swim.
He asked me, “Mortal one, did you see this?” Then he led me back to the bank of the river.
When I came back, I saw very many trees growing along both banks of the river.
He explained, “This water flows east into the countryside and runs down into the Arabah.{d} When it reaches the sea, the sea of salty water,{e} the water there becomes fresh.

Wherever the river{f} goes, every kind of living thing that moves will live. Fish will fill it in huge numbers, since the salt water turns fresh when this water arrives. Everything will live wherever the river flows.
Fishermen will line the shore, from En-gedi{g} to En-eglaim.{h} Nets will be spread out there to dry. The fish will be of many kinds, as many as in the Great Sea.{i}
But the swamps and pools beside it will not become fresh. They will be left for salt.

Along both banks of the river, all kinds of fruit trees will grow. Their leaves will never dry up, and their fruit will never run out. Each month they will bear new fruit, because the water that feeds them flows from the holy place. People will eat the fruit, and the leaves will heal.”
The Lord Yahweh says: “These{j} are the borders by which you will divide the land among Israel’s twelve tribes. Joseph will receive two shares.{k}
You will divide it equally, each tribe getting the same as the others. In an oath, I lifted My hand to give this land to your ancestors, and now it will become your inheritance.
“This is the border of the land. On the north side, it begins at the Great Sea and follows the road by Hethlon to Lebo-hamath.{l} Then it goes to Zedad,{m}
Berothah and Sibraim lie on the border between Damascus and Hamath. It goes on to Hazer-hatticon,{n} next to the border of Hauran.
So the border runs from the sea to Hazar-enon,{o} with the lands of Damascus and Hamath to the north. That makes up{p} the north side.

“The east side runs between Hauran and Damascus. Then it follows the Jordan River between Gilead and the land of Israel, from the northern border down to the eastern sea, ending at Tamar.{q} That is the east side.
“The south side runs from Tamar south to the waters of Meribath-kadesh.{r} From there it follows the Brook of Egypt{s} to the Great Sea. This is the south side, facing the Negev.
“The west side is the Great Sea itself, up to the point across from Lebo-hamath. This is the west side.
“You will divide this land among yourselves by the tribes of Israel.

You will give it out by lot as an inheritance for yourselves and for the foreigners living among you, who have raised children among you. You will treat them like people born in Israel. They will receive their shares by lot along with you, among the tribes of Israel.

verses.text: “Here are the tribes by name. In the far north, Dan will have a share. It runs along the Hethlon road toward Lebo-hamath, as far as Hazar-enan,{a} on the border of Damascus, with Hamath to the north. It stretches from the east side to the west side.{b}
Next to Dan, Asher will have one share, running from east to west.
Next to Asher, Naphtali will have one share, running from east to west.
Manasseh will have a share beside Naphtali’s, running from east to west.
Beside Manasseh, Ephraim will have a share, running from east to west.
Reuben’s share lies next to Ephraim’s, and it too runs from east to west.
Beside Reuben, Judah will have a share that runs from east to west.

“Next to Judah’s land, from the east side to the west side, will be the holy district you must set aside. Its width will be about 8.3 miles.{c} Its length from east to west will match the length of a tribe’s share. In the middle of it will stand the holy place.
The share you set apart for Yahweh will be about 8.3 miles long and about 3.3 miles{d} wide.{e}

This holy share will belong to the priests. It will measure about 8.3 miles on the north side, about 3.3 miles on the west side, about 3.3 miles on the east side, and about 8.3 miles on the south side.{f} Yahweh’s holy place will stand in the middle of it.
It is for the priests who were set apart, the descendants of Zadok. They kept faith with Me and guarded what I gave them to guard. They did not wander away as the Levites did when Israel went astray.
It will be a special gift for them from the holy share of the land. It is most holy, and it lies next to the Levites’ land.
“Beside the land of the priests, the Levites will receive a share about 8.3 miles long and about 3.3 miles wide. The whole length will be about 8.3 miles, and the width about 3.3 miles.{g}{h}
Selling or swapping any part of it is forbidden. This best part of the land may never pass into other hands,{i} because it is holy to Yahweh.
“The leftover strip, about 1.7 miles wide and about 8.3 miles long,{j} will be for everyday use by the city, for houses and for open land. In the middle of the strip will be the city.
The city will measure about 1.5 miles on the north side, about 1.5 miles on the south side,{k} about 1.5 miles on the east side, and about 1.5 miles on the west side.{l}
The open land around the city will be about 438 feet on the north, 438 feet on the south, 438 feet on the east, and 438 feet on the west.{m}

What is left along the length of the holy share will be about 3.3 miles on the east and about 3.3 miles on the west.{n} It will run beside the holy share, and its crops will feed the workers of the city.
The city’s workers, who come from all the tribes of Israel, will work its fields.
The whole share you set apart will be a square, about 8.3 miles on each side.{o} You will set apart the holy share together with the city’s land.{p}

“Whatever is left on both sides of the holy share and the city’s land will belong to the prince. It will reach east from the 8.3 miles of the holy share to the eastern border, and west from the 8.3 miles to the western border.{q} It lies next to the tribes’ shares, and it will belong to the prince. The holy share, with the temple’s holy place, will be in the middle of it.
So the Levites’ land and the city’s land will lie in the middle of the prince’s land. The prince’s land will lie between Judah’s land and Benjamin’s land.
“Now for the other tribes. Benjamin will have one share, from the east side to the west side.
Simeon will have a share beside Benjamin’s, running from east to west.
Issachar’s share is next to Simeon’s, and it runs from east to west too.
Zebulun will receive a share beside Issachar’s, running from east to west.
Beside Zebulun, Gad will have a share that runs from east to west.
Gad’s southern border will run from Tamar to the waters of Meribath-kadesh. From there it follows the Brook of Egypt to the Great Sea.
“This is the land you will give to the tribes of Israel as their own. These are their shares,” says the Lord Yahweh.
“These are the exits of the city. The north side measures about 1.5 miles.{r}
The city’s gates will carry the names of the tribes of Israel. Three gates face north, named for Reuben, Judah, and Levi.
The east side, about 1.5 miles long,{s} has three gates, named for Joseph, Benjamin, and Dan.
The south side, about 1.5 miles long,{t} has three gates, named for Simeon, Issachar, and Zebulun.
The west side, about 1.5 miles long,{u} has three gates, named for Gad, Asher, and Naphtali.
Around the city, the distance will be about 6 miles.{v} From that day on, the name of the city will be Yahweh-shammah, which means Yahweh Is There.”{w}
